jobs.description:
About Figure

Figure Technology Solutions, Inc. (Nasdaq: FIGR; OPEN: FGRS) is the leading blockchain-native capital marketplace for the origination, funding, sale and trading of tokenized assets. More than 480 partners use its loan origination system and capital marketplace. Collectively, Figure and its partners have originated over $30 billion of loans to date, among other products. The fastest growing components are Figure Connect, its credit marketplace, and Democratized Prime, Figure’s on-chain lend-borrow marketplace. Figure’s ecosystem also includes DART (Digital Asset Registry Technology) for asset custody and lien perfection, and $YLDS, a yield-bearing stablecoin registered with the SEC as a security under the Securities Act of 1933.

Figure is the market leader in real-world asset (RWA) tokenization. The company has received triple-A ratings from S&P and Moody’s on multiple loan securitizations, the first of its kind for blockchain finance.

We’re proud to be recognized as one of Forbes’ Top 50 Fintech Companies and CNBC’s World’s Top Fintech Companies.

About the Role

Figure is looking for a Principal Product Designer to help shape the future of our financial products, with a primary focus on Figure Markets and opportunities to work across our broader lending ecosystem.

This is a senior individual contributor role for a designer who thrives in complex, ambiguous problem spaces. You will work on products that span investing, lending, borrowing, digital assets, capital markets, and emerging financial infrastructure, often in areas where the product model itself is still being defined.

You will partner closely with Product, Engineering, and business leaders to turn complicated financial concepts, technical constraints, regulatory requirements, and evolving customer needs into experiences that feel clear, intuitive, and trustworthy.

We are looking for someone who can move fluidly between big-picture product thinking and detailed execution. You should be comfortable challenging assumptions, identifying gaps in requirements, working through downstream logic and edge cases, and helping a team determine not just how a feature should work, but what the right product experience should be. At the Principal level, your impact should extend beyond the projects directly assigned to you. You will help establish patterns, improve how teams approach difficult design problems, mentor other designers, and raise the quality of product design across Figure.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead product design for complex initiatives across Figure Markets, while contributing to shared problems and experiences across Figure Lending and other products.
  • Take ambiguous or incomplete product requirements and turn them into coherent end-to-end experiences, identifying missing logic, dependencies, edge cases, and opportunities along the way.
  • Develop a deep understanding of financial concepts, customer workflows, business models, and technical constraints in order to simplify inherently complicated products.
  • Partner closely with Product and Engineering from early problem definition through implementation, helping shape requirements rather than simply designing against them.
  • Explore multiple approaches to difficult problems, communicate tradeoffs clearly, and help teams make informed product decisions.
  • Design sophisticated workflows, data-dense interfaces, account and transaction experiences, permissions, states, and other interaction models common to financial products.
  • Think beyond the primary happy path. Anticipate error states, lifecycle changes, permissions, regulatory constraints, system behavior, and downstream consequences of design decisions.
  • Create prototypes and high-fidelity designs that make complex product ideas tangible and help teams align quickly.
  • Work within and contribute to Figure’s evolving design system, identifying opportunities to establish reusable patterns without forcing unique product problems into generic solutions.
  • Partner closely with Engineering during implementation to preserve intent, resolve unexpected constraints, and maintain a high bar for product quality.
  • Use research, customer feedback, product data, domain expertise, and cross-functional input to inform design decisions.
  • Present work clearly to partners and senior leadership, explaining not only what you designed but how you arrived at the solution.
  • Provide thoughtful critique and mentorship to other designers, helping raise the quality of both the work and the thinking behind it.
  • Identify patterns and opportunities that span individual products, helping Figure create more coherent experiences across Markets, Lending, and future product areas.

What We Look For

  • 8+ years of product design experience, including significant experience owning complex products or major product areas.
  • A portfolio demonstrating strong product thinking, interaction design, and visual craft across real, shipped experiences.
  • A track record of solving complicated problems where requirements, customer needs, or the underlying product model were not fully defined at the outset.
  • Strong systems thinking and an ability to understand how decisions in one part of a product affect workflows, states, users, and systems elsewhere.
  • Excellent interaction design skills, particularly for sophisticated workflows, data-heavy products, and multi-step experiences.
  • Strong visual design fundamentals and a high bar for typography, hierarchy, layout, information density, interaction detail, and overall product polish.
  • The ability to independently drive work from early problem framing through detailed design and implementation.
  • Comfort working closely with engineers and understanding enough about technical systems to make pragmatic design decisions.
  • Strong communication and storytelling skills, including the ability to explain complicated concepts and design rationale to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Experience influencing Product and Engineering partners and constructively challenging requirements when a better customer or product outcome is possible.
  • A collaborative mindset and the ability to give and receive direct, thoughtful critique.
  • A customer-first approach that prioritizes clarity, trust, and usability over novelty or personal aesthetic preference.
  • Adhere to all company security policies and data handling procedures.
  • Complete mandatory security awareness training within required timeframes.
  • Promptly report any suspected security incidents or suspicious activity to the Security team.

Nice to Have

  • Experience designing fintech, trading, investing, lending, crypto, capital markets, payments, or other financial products.
  • Experience working in regulated industries where compliance, permissions, disclosures, and operational constraints meaningfully affect the product experience.
  • Familiarity with institutional or professional financial workflows in addition to consumer products.
  • Experience with products involving complex account structures, transaction lifecycles, roles and permissions, or financial data.
  • Experience contributing to design systems and establishing reusable product patterns across teams.
  • Familiarity with front-end technologies and modern product development workflows.
  • Experience using prototyping and emerging AI tools to explore ideas, accelerate iteration, or improve the design and development process.

How You'll Make an Impact

Success in this role is not measured by the number of screens you produce. It is measured by your ability to bring clarity to difficult problems, improve the decisions a team makes, and create products that make sophisticated financial capabilities understandable and usable. You will help Figure build products that can support increasing complexity without feeling increasingly complicated, while raising the standard for product thinking and execution across the organization.

Salary

  • Base Compensation Range: $158,400 - $237,600/yr
  • 25% annual bonus target, paid quarterly
  • Company equity in the form of RSUs

This is the compensation range for the role in the United States. Actual compensation may vary based on a candidate’s experience, skills, location, internal equity, and evolving business needs. While most offers are generally made within the middle of the range, final compensation is determined based on the factors above.

  • Company HSA, FSA, Dependent Care FSA, 401(k), and commuter benefits

Hi, thanks for checking out our job board!
If you're an entrepreneurial-minded builder who loves to work with great people to solve wicked problems that have a meaningful impact, read on to see if this position might be a good fit for you!

⚡ What we’re doing

We are on a mission to eliminate bottlenecks and revolutionize the food and beverage CPG supply chain by developing innovative, all-in-one software that starts with the contract manufacturer.
Contract manufacturers and contract packagers (collectively, co-packers) are facilities that have extra production capacity and provide their services for a fee to customers (brands). Co-packers play a vital role in the trillion dollar U.S. Food and Beverage (F&B) Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG) industry, providing a range of services to convert raw materials into finished goods. jobs.description:
Company Overview

Immunome is a clinical-stage targeted oncology company committed to developing first-in-class and best-in-class targeted cancer therapies. We are advancing an innovative portfolio of therapeutics, supported by a leadership team with deep experience in the design, development, and commercialization of cutting-edge therapies, including antibody-drug conjugates. Our pipeline includes varegacestat, an investigational gamma secretase inhibitor for which an NDA has been accepted by the U.S. FDA; IM-1021, a clinical-stage ROR1 ADC; IM-1617, a clinical-stage solid tumor ADC; and IM-3050, a clinical-stage FAP-targeted radioligand therapy. We are also advancing a broad portfolio of early-stage ADCs pursuing undisclosed solid tumor targets.

Position Overview

Immunome is seeking a highly experienced and strategic National Account Director, Enterprise Access to lead integrated account strategy across a U.S. national footprint in support of our oncology portfolio. This role will build and sustain relationships with national and regional health plans, pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs), and Key Account customer networks to advance launch readiness, appropriate coverage and reimbursement, formulary access, and therapeutic adoption following regulatory approval.

The successful candidate will bring deep expertise in payer access and institutional purchasing, recognizing the distinct operating models, decision processes, and account economics of each. This position combines direct account ownership, strategic negotiation, and executive relationship management with cross-functional leadership, serving as a primary resource for field teams and connecting headquarters strategy with local execution.

Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

  • Develop and execute multi-year Payer / PBM and Key Account institution plans with defined access objectives, stakeholder engagement, procurement strategies, and measures of success.
  • Apply commercial, Medicare Part D, and Medicaid expertise alongside community and integrated delivery network (IDN) business acumen, tailoring strategies to payer coverage decisions and provider purchasing structures.
  • Translate oncology market trends, clinical differentiation, reimbursement, and clinical pathway dynamics into national account priorities and commercial planning.

Payer Access and Stakeholder Management

  • Build executive-level relationships with pharmacy directors, medical directors, clinical leaders, and pharmacy and therapeutics (P&T) decision-makers across national and regional health plans and PBMs.
  • Navigate formulary and preferred drug list (PDL) development, utilization management, and coverage and reimbursement policies across commercial plans, Medicare Part D, and Medicaid fee-for-service (FFS) programs and managed care organizations (MCOs).
  • Map decision authority and payer affiliates; coordinate internal account teams to identify access barriers, align engagement, and advance appropriate coverage outcomes.

Institutional Access and Stakeholder Management

  • Build relationships with CEOs, CFOs, COOs, medical directors, pharmacists, and practice administrators across oncology customers and their member organizations.
  • Extend engagement to IDNs, health systems, hospital and community oncology networks, and national clinical pathway organizations, aligning corporate relationships with local customer needs.
  • Use approved clinical and economic evidence to support appropriate preferred formulary and pathway positioning with relevant provider and pathway decision-makers, respecting independent clinical decisions.

Strategic Negotiation

  • Lead payer, PBM, and community account strategy and negotiations, including pull-through opportunity, within approved authority; balance coverage and purchasing objectives, rebate commitments, pricing dynamics, and long-term business value.
  • Partner with Market Access, Finance, Legal, and Compliance to evaluate contract economics, 340B considerations, and Medicaid Best Price implications and secure approvals before commitments.
  • Prepare negotiation strategies for sophisticated counterparties, execute approved agreements, and coordinate implementation, performance monitoring, and renewals.
  • Translate local access and coverage landscape into coordinated field pull-through plans, with clear account responsibilities and adherence to company policies.

Value Communication and Market Intelligence

  • Partner with Medical Affairs and health economics and outcomes research (HEOR) colleagues to translate clinical and economic evidence into account-specific value narratives using approved materials and appropriate scientific support.
  • Tailor compliant communications to payer evidence needs, population priorities, and coverage considerations, and to Key Account, provider, and pathway stakeholders’ clinical and business priorities.
  • Monitor formularies, utilization management, coverage policies, clinical pathways, and oncology market developments; synthesize account insights and evidence gaps into actionable recommendations for internal teams.

Leadership and Collaboration

  • Serve as the primary payer and corporate accounts resource for field sales, connecting headquarters strategy, national agreements, and local execution.
  • Partner with Commercial field and Market Access colleagues on shared accounts, aligning priorities, responsibilities, customer messaging, and coordinated action plans; provide proactive consultation to Sales, Marketing, Medical Affairs, HEOR, Finance, Legal, and Policy.
  • Lead cross-functional account teams and mentor colleagues, fostering accountability, consensus building, and coordinated execution without relying on direct reporting authority.

Launch Planning and Execution

  • Lead payer and key institutional account launch readiness, aligning access strategies, contracting timelines, stakeholder engagement, and field execution with applicable regulatory approvals.
  • Develop and execute educational programs through all available channels with appropriate internal partners and review processes, maintaining separation between commercial and medical activities.
  • Tailor rare disease and rare oncology launch strategies to clinical differentiation and account needs rather than relying on approaches designed for large, high-volume therapeutic classes.

Qualifications

  • Significant biopharmaceutical market access or commercial experience managing national or major regional payer accounts and national oncology GPOs.
  • Experience across commercial, Medicare Part D, and Medicaid FFS and MCO markets, as well as community and IDN purchasing structures.
  • Proven account-planning success, senior stakeholder relationships, and appropriate coverage, formulary or pathway outcomes and field pull-through.
  • Experience leading payer, PBM, and oncology negotiations and evaluating pricing and contracting implications with Finance and Legal.
  • Experience communicating clinical and HEOR evidence with Medical Affairs support and developing educational programs through appropriate channels.
  • Demonstrated success working in a highly matrixed environment influencing cross-functional strategy, and coaching or mentoring colleagues.
  • Prior product-launch experience required, including account readiness and coordinated field execution.
  • Rare disease or rare oncology experience strongly preferred, with examples of account differentiation from large, high-volume therapeutic classes.
  • Ability to engage customers nationally; ability to travel up to 50%.

Knowledge and Skills

  • Deep knowledge of payer and PBM business models, revenues and incentives, and how insurance-side coverage differs from community and IDN purchasing.
  • Knowledge of formulary and PDL development, utilization management, reimbursement policies, and provider formulary and clinical pathway decisions.
  • Financial and contracting acumen across rebates, pricing, 340B, Medicaid Best Price, and key account economics.
  • Deep oncology therapeutic-area knowledge, including biologic and biosimilar access dynamics where relevant.
  • Ability to translate clinical and HEOR evidence into account-specific value narratives and identify evidence gaps with subject matter experts.
  • Executive presence, sound judgment, negotiation, stakeholder mapping, and relationship management skills across complex payer and provider accounts.
  • Cross-functional leadership and influence, including consultation, consensus building, mentoring, and collaboration across headquarters and field teams.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, strategic planning, and problem-solving skills; accountability and effective prioritization in a dynamic biotech environment.

Corporate IT Manager

Who We Are

Yuno is the AI-native operating system of global commerce, powering the financial infrastructure of enterprise merchants, banks, and wallets. Through a single API, Yuno connects them to pay-ins, payouts, fraud prevention, KYC/KYB, and stablecoins globally, so they can operate everywhere. Global brands including McDonald's, NetEase Games, GoFundMe, and Rappi run their payments on Yuno.

About The Role

Yuno is looking for a Corporate IT Manager, based in India, to own the internal technology backbone that keeps our fully remote, global team productive and secure. From device management and identity to SaaS administration and compliance, you'll lead Corporate IT, a new area within our Tech Infrastructure team, designing systems and automation that scale as Yuno grows across 190+ countries.

This is not a helpdesk role. You'll own the corporate IT stack end to end, drive the roadmap, automate what others still do by hand, and make security and compliance a built-in default rather than an afterthought — which matters when the company runs payments for global brands. You'll work closely with our Security team, taking corporate IT workload off SecOps, and you'll build and lead the Corporate IT team as it grows.

How AI Shows Up in This Role

  • You'll build AI-driven automation for IT and helpdesk, turning repetitive requests and lifecycle workflows into self-serve flows, and maintain machine-readable documentation that AI assistants can act on
  • As an AI-native company, Yuno runs on a growing stack of AI tools — you'll own how they're provisioned, secured, and governed across the org, managing access and OAuth/shadow-AI risk. And you're encouraged to use AI to move faster in your own work

Your Contribution Will Be

  • Corporate IT ownership and roadmap — own the corporate IT function end to end and drive the corporate IT roadmap as the company scales
  • Device and endpoint management — own the MDM platform (Jamf, Intune, or Kandji) for a distributed macOS and Windows fleet: zero-touch provisioning, patching, configuration-as-code, and endpoint security
  • Identity and access management — administer the identity provider (Okta or equivalent), SSO, MFA, and SCIM; automate onboarding and offboarding, and enforce least-privilege access across every system
  • SaaS administration and governance — manage the SaaS stack (Google Workspace, Slack, Atlassian, and more), rein in shadow IT and OAuth risk, and right-size licenses and access
  • Security and compliance — build and maintain the controls, access reviews, and audit evidence that keep Yuno compliant (SOC 2, PCI DSS, ISO 27001), partnering with Security on vendor reviews
  • Automation — replace manual work with scripting and workflow automation (Python, Okta Workflows, or similar)
  • Team leadership and enablement — act as the senior escalation point for complex IT issues, maintain clear runbooks and documentation, and lead and mentor the Corporate IT team as it grows

What Success Looks Like

Within your first 6–12 months, onboarding and offboarding run end to end without manual steps, the device fleet and SaaS access are fully managed and auditable, and SOC 2 and PCI evidence is something the team produces continuously rather than scrambling for at audit time.

Skills You Need

Minimum Qualifications

  • 5+ years in corporate IT, IT operations, or IT systems engineering, ideally supporting a distributed workforce
  • Experience managing or mentoring IT team members, or leading corporate IT for a team or company
  • Based in India, with the right to work in India
  • MDM expertise — hands-on with Jamf Pro, Intune, or Kandji for macOS and Windows fleet management
  • Identity and access management — managing an identity provider (Okta strongly preferred), SSO, MFA, and provisioning/deprovisioning
  • SaaS administration — Google Workspace, Slack, Atlassian, and similar, with an understanding of SaaS and OAuth governance
  • Security and compliance — hands-on support for frameworks like SOC 2, ISO 27001, or PCI DSS (access reviews, audit evidence)
  • Scripting and automation — Python, JavaScript, PowerShell, or workflow tools to eliminate manual toil
  • Networking fundamentals — TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, and VPNs
  • English — advanced proficiency, written and spoken

Preferred Qualifications

  • Building AI-driven IT automation (e.g., Console.com, Risotto, Unthread) or helpdesk and agentic tooling
  • Hardware lifecycle and asset management (ITAM) at scale
  • Experience in the payments or fintech industry, where compliance and access controls are stricter
  • Familiarity with Zero Trust, PAM, and least-privilege access models

Nice to Have

  • Configuration-as-code for endpoints (an infrastructure-as-code mindset for IT)
  • Experience securing and governing AI tools or agents across an organization

What We Offer at Yuno

  • Home Office Bonus — a one-time allowance to set up your ideal home office

**Travel to Office expectations**

For Remote Roles: If this role is remote, there will be in-office events that will require travel to and from the Mississauga and/or Salt Lake City office. These will include, but not limited to, onboarding, team events, semi-annual and annual team meetings.
For Hybrid Roles: If this role is Hybrid, there will be an expectation to reside within commutable distance to the office/location specified in the job listing. This will include, but not limited to, weekly/bi-weekly/monthly events in the office with your specific team. This is a requirement for this role.

Position Summary

We are looking for a Senior Salesforce Architect, reporting to the Sr Manager- AI & Platform Architecture, to design, deliver, and continuously improve our Product-to-Cash landscape on Salesforce. This is a coaching and mentoring–focused role: you will guide engineers and solution designers, raise architectural standards, and bring deep hands-on expertise in Revenue Cloud Advanced (RCA), the billing system, and the broader quote-to-cash lifecycle.

Working in close partnership with other Architects, you will help solve complex business and technical challenges and ensure solutions are designed to best serve the evolving needs of the company. The ideal candidate pairs strong Salesforce architecture experience with an AI-first mindset, applying Agentforce and Claude-based solutions to solve problems, and the ability to identify and resolve process and technology gaps across the Product-to-Cash value chain, ensuring solutions align to their core business domains and to the enterprise taxonomy framework that underpins domain roadmaps and technology transformation.

  • Serve as the architectural coach and mentor for engineers and solution designers across the Product-to-Cash domain, building team capability in Revenue Cloud Advanced and billing

  • Produce High-Level Designs (HLD), Low-Level Designs (LLD), and conceptual diagrams that clearly communicate architecture to technical and business audiences
  • Manage architecture and system roadmaps, ensuring alignment with platform standards and the long-term direction of the Product-to-Cash landscape

  • Provide hands-on Revenue Cloud Advanced (RCA)/CPQ coaching, including configuration patterns, design trade-offs, and implementation best practices
  • Own the end-to-end architecture of the Product-to-Cash lifecycle: quoting, contracting, ordering, fulfilment, billing, invoicing, revenue, customer success, and customer support
  • Architect and govern the billing system and billing platform, ensuring accurate invoicing, billing schedules, payment handling, dunning, and revenue recognition flows
  • Identify and resolve process gaps and technology gaps across Product-to-Cash, defining remediation approaches and driving them to resolution
  • Apply an AI-first mindset to problem solving, leveraging Agentforce and Claude-based solutions where they add value
  • Work with the development team to hand over designs cleanly, ensuring they have the context and clarity needed to build
  • During project execution, work with SMEs and Product Owners to address any requirement gaps and shape the right solution
  • Extend and mature the Product-to-Cash solution as business needs evolve, ensuring the architecture scales with new products, pricing models, and billing scenarios
  • Translate business requirements into well-architected solutions that best leverage the Salesforce platform and Revenue Cloud
  • Apply architectural and engineering concepts to meet operational requirements such as scalability, maintainability, security, reliability, extensibility, availability, and manageability

  • Promote the adoption of design patterns and standard processes for solution design and development
  • Partner with data and integration architects to ensure data integrity, security, compliance, and seamless data flow between billing, ERP, and other systems
  • Work closely with solution architects to ensure individual solutions align with the overall enterprise architecture
  • Contribute to a learning community within the enterprise architecture discipline, fostering continuous improvement

Required Experience & Skills

  • Demonstrated ability to identify and resolve process gaps and technology gaps across the Product-to-Cash value chain
  • An AI-first mindset, with exposure to Agent force and Claude-based solutions for solving business and technical problems
  • Experience working with Salesforce Connected Apps (applications from the Salesforce AppExchange)
  • Proven experience designing and delivering complex B2B SaaS Salesforce solutions
  • Familiarity with managed packages such as Gong, DocuSign CLM, Kantata, Gainsight, Showpad, Qualtrics, or similar enterprise apps is a plus

Annual OTE Salary
$88,230—$129,750 USD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. jobs.description:
About Zuma

Zuma is pioneering the future of agentic AI and our focus is to transform the rental market experience for consumers and property manager alike. Our innovative platform is engineered from the ground up to boost operations efficiency and enhance support capabilities for property management business across the US and Canada, a ~$200B market.
Off the back of our Series-A in early 2024, Zuma is scaling rapidly. Achieving our vision requires a team of passionate, innovative individuals eager to leverage technology to redefine customer-business interactions. We're on the hunt for exceptional talent ready to join our mission and contribute to building a groundbreaking technology that reshapes how businesses engage with customers.
Zuma has raised over $17M in funding to date and has support from world-renowned investors, including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Y Combinator, King River, Range Ventures, and distinguished angel investors like YC’s former COO, Qasar Younis.

The Role

As a Support Engineer at Zuma, you’ll be a bridge between our customers, engineering team, and product vision. You’ll ensure new customers onboard smoothly, integrations run reliably, and support operations scale as we grow. This is a hands-on role for someone who loves problem-solving, can dive into APIs and databases, and takes pride in clear documentation and communication. You’ll help property managers succeed with our AI platform while also driving continuous improvements in our internal tools and processes.

Why This Could Be Your Dream Role

  • You want to work at a company where customers feel your impact every day
  • You'll have autonomy to design and implement innovative technical solutions
  • Your work will directly impact thousands of apartment communities and millions of renters
  • You'll receive significant equity in a venture-backed company with strong traction
  • As we scale, your role and influence will grow with the company

Why You Might Want to Think Twice

  • This is a demanding role that will often require extended hours and deep commitment
  • As a founding team member, you'll need to wear multiple hats and step outside your comfort zone
  • You'll need to make thoughtful tradeoffs between innovation and immediate needs
  • You'll interact directly with customers to understand their needs and occasionally travel to their offices
  • We're a startup - priorities can shift rapidly as we respond to market opportunities and customer needs
  • If you're not comfortable getting your hands dirty with legacy code or speaking directly with customers, this isn't the job for you

Responsibilities

  • Lead critical system rewrites to transform our architecture into a highly scalable, resilient foundation
  • Own the design and performance optimization of our data storage systems, ensuring they scale with customer and AI demands
  • Build and evolve our deployment pipelines, enabling reliable, automated releases for AI-first products
  • Set up and manage modern cloud infrastructure from scratch, leveraging Infrastructure as Code (IaC) to ensure consistency, security, and scalability
  • Establish engineering best practices, including observability, incident response processes, and system hardening for an AI-first platform
  • Drive robust analytics and monitoring to track performance, reliability, and the effectiveness of our AI solutions
  • Mentor engineers and elevate the team's capabilities across infrastructure, scalability, and AI product development

Your Experience Looks Like

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field
  • 3+ years of experience building production-grade software systems, with a focus on scalability, performance, and reliability
  • Proven expertise in backend development with , including API design, system architecture, and cloud-based services
  • Experience with cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, or similar) and deploying production systems using Infrastructure as Code (e.g., Terraform, Pulumi)
  • Hands-on experience with database design, performance tuning, and scaling high-throughput data systems
  • Familiarity with building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, and modern DevOps practices
  • Strong communication skills and ability to work effectively in a distributed, fast-paced environment
  • Comfortable operating in early-stage, high-ownership environments with evolving requirements
  • Bonus: Experience with React and TypeScript on the frontend, though this role leans backend/infrastructure
  • Bonus: Exposure to LLM-based systems, AI infrastructure, or agentic AI workflows

Guiding Principles

    Customer‑First Outcomes

    Every commit should trace back to resident or operator value. Whether it’s a new feature, infra investment, or AI capability, if it doesn’t solve a real problem, it doesn’t ship.

    Bias for Simplicity

    We favor composable primitives over clever abstractions. Open standards, clean APIs, and clear contracts win over custom complexity, even if the custom version is cooler.

    Quality Is a Gate, Not an After‑Thought

    Quality is built-in from day one. Our definition of done includes: test coverage, performance checks, basic observability, and internal docs. Shipping fast doesn’t mean skipping craftsmanship.

    Data‑Driven Choices

    We use data to guide, not paralyze, our decision-making. We track leading indicators (cycle time, defect rate, NPS) and lagging signals (retention, revenue impact). We keep instrumentation lightweight but meaningful signal over spreadsheet.

    Transparency & Written Culture

    Good ideas don’t expire in Zoom. We operate in public inside the company, TDDs, PR reviews, and Linear tickets tell the story. This keeps us async-friendly, auditable, and aligned across time zones and functions.

Other Benefits

  • Great health insurance, dental, and vision.
  • Gym and workspace stipends.
  • Computer and workspace enhancements.
  • Unlimited PTO.
  • Opportunity to play a critical role in building the foundations of the company and Engineering culture.

As a senior overlay seller and specialized leader, you will partner closely with SaaS Account Executives to define and execute strategic account plans, solve significant and unique customer challenges, and expand media revenue across high value enterprise accounts. You will operate with substantial independence, establish the methods for new or special assignments, and create alignment across internal and customer stakeholder groups.

This is an opportunity to influence how 6sense approaches complex advertising opportunities, contribute thought leadership to a growing business, and drive outcomes across one of the company’s expanding revenue streams.

What You’ll Do

  • Own the strategy and execution of significant, complex enterprise advertising sales motions across strategic accounts, from opportunity creation through close and expansion.
  • Serve as a specialized advertising leader for customers and internal partners, bringing thought leadership to high impact pursuits and helping shape repeatable approaches for complex opportunities.
  • Build formal networks with executive marketing buyers and key stakeholders across advertising, media, demand generation, account based marketing, procurement, finance, and other customer groups.
  • Evaluate tangible and intangible factors across business priorities, customer dynamics, audience strategy, data, competition, and commercial terms to determine the best path to results.
  • Create tailored value narratives that connect programmatic advertising, audience activation, predictive intelligence, intent data, and AI powered insights to pipeline, revenue, account engagement, and broader business outcomes.
  • Expand media revenue by identifying new buying centers, developing executive relationships, navigating matrixed organizations, and increasing share of wallet across strategic enterprise accounts.
  • Partner across Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, Product, and other functions to coordinate account strategy, remove barriers, and align resources around shared customer outcomes.
  • Act independently to define methods and procedures for new or special assignments, while guiding or coordinating the activities of others as needed to advance complex pursuits.
  • Capture field insights, influence sales practices, and develop scalable approaches that strengthen the advertising business beyond an individual account portfolio.

Requirements

  • 12 or more years of relevant enterprise advertising or SaaS sales experience with a bachelor’s degree, or 8 or more years with a master’s degree. Equivalent practical experience will also be considered.
  • Broad expertise or unique knowledge in B2B programmatic advertising, including capabilities such as audience targeting, predictive intelligence, intent data, or AI powered marketing.
  • Proven success selling into large, complex enterprise organizations, preferably Fortune 500 companies.
  • Demonstrated record of meeting or exceeding quota and closing complex six figure and seven figure deals.
  • Experience leading significant and unique sales opportunities where success requires evaluating intangible factors, exercising independent judgment, and defining the appropriate strategy and methods.
  • Proven ability to expand revenue across complex enterprise organizations through executive relationship development, new buying center identification, multiple stakeholder engagement, and cross functional alignment.
  • Ability to create alignment across formal stakeholder networks and influence senior internal and external decision makers without relying on direct authority.
  • Strong executive presence, consultative selling capability, commercial judgment, business acumen, and communication skills.
  • Ability to translate advertising, audience, data, and AI capabilities into measurable pipeline, revenue, and customer business outcomes.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience engaging CMOs and senior leaders across Marketing, Advertising, Media, Demand Generation, and Account Based Marketing.
  • Experience operating as an overlay seller or subject matter leader in partnership with SaaS Account Executives across strategic enterprise accounts.
  • Experience shaping new sales motions, developing repeatable practices, or influencing how teams pursue complex enterprise advertising opportunities.
  • Experience coordinating the work of cross functional contributors on high impact pursuits or special assignments.

The Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is a specialized individual contributor with broad enterprise advertising expertise and the judgment to solve significant, unique, and strategically important customer challenges. This person is comfortable evaluating ambiguity and intangible factors, determining the right approach without a predefined playbook, and creating alignment across complex stakeholder networks.

They have successfully sold B2B programmatic advertising into large enterprise organizations and understand how advertising fits within a broader B2B go to market strategy. They combine executive credibility with hands on sales execution, connect investments to measurable business outcomes, and contribute thought leadership and scalable practices that improve results beyond their individual accounts.

Position Summary

  • Extend and mature the Product-to-Cash solution as business needs evolve, ensuring the architecture scales with new products, pricing models, and billing scenarios
  • Translate business requirements into well-architected solutions that best leverage the Salesforce platform and Revenue Cloud
  • Apply architectural and engineering concepts to meet operational requirements such as scalability, maintainability, security, reliability, extensibility, availability, and manageability
  • Conduct research and develop Proof of Concepts on emerging Salesforce and billing capabilities, recommending solutions that are functionally robust and cost-effective
  • Promote the adoption of design patterns and standard processes for solution design and development
  • Partner with data and integration architects to ensure data integrity, security, compliance, and seamless data flow between billing, ERP, and other systems
  • Work closely with solution architects to ensure individual solutions align with the overall enterprise architecture
  • Contribute to a learning community within the enterprise architecture discipline, fostering continuous improvement

Required Experience & Skills

  • Experience working with integration teams to design and govern cross-system integrations
  • Demonstrated ability to identify and resolve process gaps and technology gaps across the Product-to-Cash value chain
  • An AI-first mindset, with exposure to Agent force and Claude-based solutions for solving business and technical problems
  • Experience working with Salesforce Connected Apps (applications from the Salesforce AppExchange)
  • Proven experience designing and delivering complex B2B SaaS Salesforce solutions
  • Familiarity with managed packages such as Gong, DocuSign CLM, Kantata, Gainsight, Showpad, Qualtrics, or similar enterprise apps is a plus

At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

You will lead regular account planning sessions and build the full mix of ABM tactics against your target accounts, partnering with digital, content, demand generation, and field marketing teams to bring personalized experiences to the full buying committee across the buyer's journey. Our North America ABM program is organized around the motions that drive Enterprise growth: winning new logos, progressing active opportunities, expanding existing customers, and growing alongside our partners.

This is a highly cross-functional role that requires close partnership across Sales, Marketing, Product Marketing, and Marketing Operations, as well as strong written and verbal communication skills.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US.

About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The role

We are looking for a Technical Project Manager to own server and rack-level production projects for large-scale AI datacenter infrastructure. This role connects capacity planning, hardware architecture, procurement, ODM manufacturing, logistics, and datacenter deployment teams. You will make sure the right GPU, compute, and storage infrastructure is ordered, produced, delivered, and deployed on time. The role requires strong server hardware knowledge, structured project management, vendor coordination, and high ownership across adjacent work-streams.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Align server and rack requirements with capacity planning and datacenter architecture teams. Translate project demand into hardware inputs for procurement and ODM production.
  • Decompose required key parts, including CPUs, memory, drives, NICs, and other critical components. Validate that procured components are compatible with required server configurations.
  • Place and track production orders with ODM partners. Coordinate BOM readiness, component availability, and production timelines.
  • Manage a portfolio of production projects across multiple projects and vendors. Track risks, blockers, dependencies, and recovery plans.
  • Escalate issues early, including BOM problems, shortages, quality risks, factory delays, payment delays, export license issues, and deployment schedule changes. Visit factories when needed to support quality control, production execution, and timeline recovery.
  • Track adjacent processes such as POs, invoices, export licenses, payments, logistics bookings, and required documentation.
  • Provide regular production status, risk updates, and decision points to stakeholders.
  • Drive issue resolution across planning, procurement, production, testing, logistics, delivery, and deployment.
  • Continious improvements after each production cycle. Improve ODM requirements, supplier expectations, internal processes, reporting, and tooling. Gather deployment and operations feedback and convert it into future production improvements.

We expect you to have:

  • Experience managing complex hardware production, manufacturing, supply chain, infrastructure, or datacenter delivery projects.
  • Strong understanding of modern server architectures, especially high-performance GPU-based environments.
  • Knowledge of server components and ability to configure hardware for different service needs.
  • Ability to quickly adapt to new server platforms, components, and technologies.
  • Experience working with ODMs, OEMs, factories, hardware vendors, or contract manufacturers.
  • Experience with BOMs, component planning, production timelines, and factory execution.
  • Strong project management skills, including Gantt charts, milestones, dependencies, and risk tracking.
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and ability to work under tight deadlines.
  • Strong communication, negotiation, and vendor management skills.
  • High ownership, structured thinking, and ability to drive work-streams outside the narrow TPM scope.

It will be an added bonus if you have:

  • Basic understanding of GPU infrastructure including diagnostics/troubleshooting of GPU.
  • Ability to collect system logs and hardware diagnostics, with a general understanding of BIOS/BMC functionality and their interaction with the operating system and hardware components.

  • Career growth and learning opportunities
  • Flexibility and ownership
  • Collaborative and innovative culture
  • Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

jobs.excerpt: Mactores is the agent-native AWS modernization firm.
jobs.description:
Mactores is the agent-native AWS modernization firm. Most modernization work doesn't ship, it stalls in pilots, slips a year, or lands at three times the budget. We exist to ship it: production systems running, legacy retired, outcomes measured. Our delivery is built on Aedeon, the agent platform built by Mactores' founders' sister company, which absorbs the repetitive 60–70% of engagement work, discovery, dependency mapping, validation, test generation, that traditional consulting bills human hours against. Forward-deployed engineers own the rest: architecture, judgment, and cutover, on dates we commit to in the contract.

We are seeking an experienced Senior Database Developer to lead and support Oracle to PostgreSQL/Aurora PostgreSQL migration initiatives. The role involves deep hands-on work across SQL refactoring, schema conversion, DMS operations, performance tuning, and post–go-live stabilization. The candidate will work closely with application teams, cloud engineers, and stakeholders to ensure a smooth, performant, and compliant migration.

What you will do?

  • Refactor and convert Oracle SQL, PL/SQL, and database objects to PostgreSQL-compatible SQL/PLpgSQL.
  • Analyze and remediate AWS SCT (Schema Conversion Tool) findings and limitations.
  • Manage and maintain Flyway migration codebase (versioned scripts, repeatable migrations, rollbacks).
  • Identify, troubleshoot, and fix database-related application bugs.
  • Perform query optimization for PostgreSQL (execution plans, indexing strategies, query rewrites).
  • Support and monitor AWS DMS during full load and CDC phases.
  • Diagnose and resolve DMS data and performance issues.
  • Perform data validation and reconciliation between Oracle and PostgreSQL.

JOB DESCRIPTION

RENEWAL RISK ENGINEER, [Management Liability]

Counterpart is an insurtech platform reimagining management and professional liability for the modern workplace. We believe that when businesses lead with clarity and confidence, they become more resilient, more innovative, and better prepared for what’s ahead. That’s why we built the first Agentic Insurance™ system — where advanced AI and deep insurance expertise come together to proactively assess, mitigate, and manage risk. Backed by A rated carriers and trusted by brokers nationwide, our platform helps small businesses grow with confidence. Join us in shaping a smarter future, helping businesses Do More With Less Risk®.

Counterpart is the place for people who want to build and use top-tier technology to improve insurance products and outcomes for small businesses. You will own real problems, work alongside the future leaders of this industry, and help build a company defining a category.

As a member of the risk engineering team, you will be responsible for the production of premium through proper risk analysis and effective distribution of our product. In collaboration with the engineering, design, data, and operations team, you will leverage your industry knowledge and broker relationships to develop management liability and professional liability insurance products that brokers are eager to promote to their clients.

AS A PRODUCTION FOCUSED RISK ENGINEER YOU WILL:

  • Underwrite renewal business across ML product lines in accordance with company guidelines and performance targets.
  • Evaluate risk exposures, loss history, and operational data to determine appropriate pricing, coverage, and terms.
  • Provide quick and competitive quotes in alignment with distribution and market strategies.
  • Serve as a trusted partner to wholesale brokers by offering thoughtful underwriting guidance and responsive communication.
    Maintain and expand a portfolio of high-performing broker relationships to drive retention and profitable growth.
  • Represent Counterpart at broker meetings, industry conferences, and networking events.
  • Work closely with fellow Risk Engineers and product teams to refine guidelines, pricing models, and coverage forms.
    Identify market feedback and recommend enhancements to improve product offerings and underwriting strategy.
  • Bind renewal accounts through consistent engagement with brokers and effective management of the renewal lifecycle.
  • Maintain accurate and compliant documentation for all underwriting decisions.

WE LOOK FOR TEAMMATES WHO HAVE:

  • 2+ years of underwriting experience in Management Liability, ideally with a focus on renewals within the wholesale distribution channel.
  • Demonstrated success in building and maintaining broker relationships.
  • Expertise in specialty liability products including policy forms, rating procedures, and coverage structures.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills.
  • Confidence in presenting and discussing underwriting decisions with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Proficiency with modern underwriting tools and systems
  • Bachelor’s degree preferred, with a minimum of 4 years of relevant work experience.
  • Professional designations (e.g., RPLU, CPCU) are a plus.

PEOPLE WHO THRIVE HERE:

  • Entrepreneurial, willing to experiment, embrace new technology, try new things
  • Comfortable with ambiguity and rapidly changing priorities. Change is normal and happens quickly at startups. You have experience experimenting, learning, and pivoting with your learnings.
  • Take ownership of your projects, your deadlines, your functions, your calendar, your own destiny. People who thrive at a startup like ours have a bias toward action and documentation.
  • Communicate directly and with clarity. Working cross-functionally is an essential part of any role at Counterpart. You’ll succeed by conjoining expectations with others and holding all accountable.

THE HARD PARTS:

  • We're early, and that's not always comfortable. Counterpart is still a young company, which means some processes, tools, and norms are still being built in real time. You may encounter situations where the answer doesn't exist yet — and you'll be expected to help create it rather than wait for someone else to.
  • The feedback culture is real. We mean it when we say speak boldly and honestly. That goes both ways — you'll be expected to give direct feedback and to receive it without defensiveness. If you've spent your career in environments where difficult conversations get softened or avoided, that adjustment can take time.
  • Distributed work requires more intentionality. There's no office to drop by, no hallway conversation to clear up a misunderstanding. Staying connected, communicating proactively, and building relationships across a remote team takes real effort — it doesn't happen automatically here.
  • We move fast and expect you to keep up. Counterpart operates with a bias toward action. Decisions get made quickly, priorities can shift, and we don't wait for perfect information. If you're used to slower, more deliberate organizational rhythms, the pace here can be a genuine adjustment.
  • You're expected to own your outcomes. There's a high degree of autonomy here, which is a feature — but it also means there's no one looking over your shoulder to catch things before they become problems. The people who thrive take that ownership seriously and hold themselves accountable without being asked.

WHO YOU WILL WORK WITH:

  • Tanner Hackett, CEO: Having founded two other major startups, including Button and Lazada, Tanner now spends his time focused on mental health through his philanthropy,, in addition to reading, surfing, yoga, and enjoying the outdoors.
  • Brad Bahler, Director of Field Underwriting: Brad has over a decade of experience in management liability underwriting. He managed one of the largest books of small business management liability risks at Travelers, where he was known for his deep understanding of coverage, outstanding submission response times, and boundless enthusiasm for the space.
  • Jake O’Donnell, Risk Engineer Territory Lead: Jake started his insurance career at Chubb, where he was able to develop and grow a profitable book of private-for-profit and non-profit management liability business. Jake is known for his exceptional service to industry brokers and his extensive knowledge of management liability. Jake also is a CPCU designation recipient.

WHAT WE OFFER

  • Fully remote workplace
  • Unlimited Vacation: We offer flexible time off, allowing you to take time when you need it.
  • Work from Anywhere: Counterpart is a fully distributed company, meaning there is no office. We allow employees to work from wherever they do their best work, and invite the team to meet in person a couple times per year.
  • Stock Options
  • Health, Dental, and Vision Coverage
  • 401(k) Retirement Plan
  • Parental Leave
  • Home Office Allowance: to set up your home office with the necessary equipment and accessories.
  • Wellness Stipend
  • Book stipend
  • Professional Development Reimbursement
  • No working birthdays: Take your birthday off, giving you the opportunity to relax, enjoy your special day, and spend time with loved ones.
  • Charitable Contribution Matching

COUNTERPART'S VALUES

  • Conjoin Expectations - it is the cornerstone of autonomy. Ensure you are aware of what is expected of you and clearly articulate what you expect of others.
  • Speak Boldly & Honestly - the only failure is not learning from mistakes. Don’t cheat yourself and your colleagues of the feedback needed when expectations aren’t being met.
  • Be Entrepreneurial - control your own destiny. Embrace action over perfection while navigating any obstacles that stand in the way of your ultimate goal.
  • Practice Omotenashi (“selfless hospitality”) - trust will follow. Consider every interaction with internal and external partners an opportunity to develop trust by going above and beyond what is expected.
  • Hold Nothing As Sacred - create routines but modify them routinely.Take the time to reflect on where the business is today, where it needs to go, and what you have to change in order to get there.
  • Prioritize Wellness - some things should never be sacrificed. We create an environment that stretches everyone to grow and improve, which is fulfilling, but is only one part of a meaningful life.

Our estimated pay range for this role is $120,000 to $160,000 total. Base salary is determined by a variety of factors, including but not limited to, market data, location, internal equitability, and experience.

We are committed to being a welcoming and inclusive workplace for everyone, and we are intentional about making sure people feel respected, supported and connected at work—regardless of who you are or where you come from. We value and celebrate our differences and we believe being open about who we are allows us to do the best work of our lives.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not discriminate against qualified applicants or employees on the basis of race, color, religion, gender identity, sex, sexual preference, sexual identity, pregnancy, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, age, marital status, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, military status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law, rule, or regulation.

jobs.title: Senior Database Administrator (Freelancer)
jobs.excerpt: Mactores is the agent-native AWS modernization firm.
jobs.description:
Mactores is the agent-native AWS modernization firm. Most modernization work doesn't ship, it stalls in pilots, slips a year, or lands at three times the budget. We exist to ship it: production systems running, legacy retired, outcomes measured. Our delivery is built on Aedeon, the agent platform built by Mactores' founders' sister company, which absorbs the repetitive 60–70% of engagement work, discovery, dependency mapping, validation, test generation, that traditional consulting bills human hours against. Forward-deployed engineers own the rest: architecture, judgment, and cutover, on dates we commit to in the contract.

Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migrations don't fail at conversion. They fail at go-live DMS latency nobody diagnosed, autovacuum behavior nobody tuned, privilege mappings nobody tested, incidents nobody owns at 2 a.m. This role sits inside our Application & Database Modernization pillar and exists to make sure that doesn't happen.

As our Senior Database Administrator, you'll run the Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL environments in an active Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration program from cluster design through DMS replication through post–go-live stabilization. Aedeon handles the repeatable conversion and validation work; you own what agents can't: production judgment. When replication lags, when a workload misbehaves after cutover, when an incident escalates past L2, you're the person who resolves it and can explain why it happened.

This is a freelance engagement, remote, working as the L3 escalation point on production systems that real businesses run on.

What you will do?

  • Design, set up, configure, and manage Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL clusters.
  • Configure parameters, maintenance windows, monitoring, and scaling strategies.
  • Keep the environments highly available, fault tolerant, and operationally ready — before go-live, not after.
  • Map users, roles, and privileges from Oracle to PostgreSQL.
  • Implement least-privilege access, role hierarchies, and security best practices, and support audit and compliance requirements.
  • Configure, run, monitor, and optimize AWS DMS tasks (Full Load and CDC).
  • Troubleshoot DMS latency, data mismatches, and performance issues, and tune DMS settings for large-volume, high-throughput workloads.
  • Tune server and database performance — CPU, memory, I/O, connections — plus PostgreSQL parameters, autovacuum, indexing, and query behavior.
  • Find performance bottlenecks before the customer does, and resolve them.
  • Design and implement backup and restore strategies; define and test DR and failover procedures; support cross-region replication and recovery drills.
  • Lead post–go-live stabilization: monitor production workloads, resolve incidents, and act as the L3 escalation point for database-related production issues.
  • Deliver operational documentation and handover support, so what you stabilized stays stable after you.

What are we looking for?

  • 5+ years of experience administering Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL.
  • Proven expertise supporting Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migrations.
  • Hands-on experience with AWS DMS.
  • Advanced PostgreSQL performance tuning and troubleshooting skills.
  • Strong knowledge of backup, restore, and DR planning in AWS.
  • Experience with AWS monitoring tools (CloudWatch, Performance Insights).
  • Strong problem-solving and root-cause analysis abilities.
  • Experience working in production and post–go-live environments.
  • The ability to work independently as an L3 escalation engineer.
  • Clear communication and documentation skills.

You will be preferred if

  • Familiarity with automation and configuration management tools, such as Ansible, Chef, or Puppet
  • Familiarity with IAAC tools such as Terraform, CloudFormation
  • Familiarity with CI/CD implementation tools like Liquibase/Flyway
  • AWS Certified Database – Specialty
  • AWS Certified Solutions Architect

How we work?

    We refactor legacy databases to cloud-native AWS on a committed date, with Mactores carrying delivery overage risk for delays we cause. Aedeon absorbs the repetitive majority schema conversion, test generation, regression harnesses. Engineers absorb the judgment: risk tradeoffs, production cutover, post-cutover optimization. You're the judgment layer for this program's production environments. When we tell a customer their database will be stable on a date, your work is what makes that sentence true.

Life at Mactores

We care about creating a culture that makes a real difference in the lives of every Mactorian. Our 10 Core Leadership Principles that honor Decision-making, Leadership, Collaboration, and Curiosity drive how we work.
1. Be one step ahead
2. Deliver the best
3. Be bold
4. Pay attention to the detail
5. Enjoy the challenge
6. Be curious and take action
7. Take leadership
8. Own it
9. Deliver value
10. Be collaborative
We would like you to read more details about the work culture on

The Path to Joining the Mactores Team

At Mactores, our recruitment process is structured around three distinct stages:

A series of evaluations of your technical proficiency and suitability for the role.
Managerial Interview: The hiring manager engages with you in multiple discussions, 30 minutes to an hour each, covering technical skills, hands-on experience, leadership potential, and communication.

About the role

Grüns is scaling fast, and our customer experience has to scale with it. As CX Operations Manager, you'll own the systems behind how our support team learns, performs, and improves: the knowledge base, training, QA, and the data that shows us where to act next. You'll partner with our BPO leadership and our AI Lead to make every agent sharper and every customer interaction faster and better.

This role is part of our remote HQ! We have a fully remote, high-trust work environment - and also come together on a quarterly basis for amazing off-sites where we can connect IRL.

In this role, you will:

  • Own our knowledge base as the single source of truth: accurate, organized, easy to use, and audited on a recurring cadence
  • Design and facilitate CX onboarding, training, and continuing education for new and tenured agents, including virtual sessions across time zones, built for every learning style
  • Dig into CSAT, NPS, QA, FCR, and AHT data to find gaps in workflows and knowledge, then turn them into specific fixes
  • Partner with our internal QA team and BPO leadership on calibrations, 1:1 coaching, and performance improvement plans, serving as the liaison between support leadership and agents
  • Build and maintain FAQs and agent macros that drive self-service and agent efficiency
  • Work with our AI Lead to identify automation and deflection opportunities, and implement internal tools that improve resolution times and CSAT

We're looking for someone who:

  • Has 5+ years in Customer Experience, Support Operations, CX Ops, QA, Training, or Knowledge Management
  • Has 2+ years in a managerial role, or an equivalent independent-contributor role with real ownership
  • Has worked directly with BPO teams
  • Has created and maintained documentation (SOPs, macros, help articles, templates) that a frontline team actually uses
  • Has mastered analyzing CX performance reporting: CSAT, quality scoring, contact drivers, first response time, and resolution quality
  • Is hands-on with a support platform (Gladly, Zendesk, Gorgias, Intercom, Salesforce Service Cloud, or similar), a knowledge tool (Notion, Confluence, Guru, or similar), and QA workflows (scorecards, sampling, calibration)
  • Is strong in Google Workspace and builds trackers and reporting in Sheets with ease (pivot tables, filters, structured logs)
  • Bonus: has used AI tools or built AI agents (Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code)

Approach to the role:

  • Runs a regimented cadence: sets the rhythm, hits deadlines, and keeps programs moving without reminders
  • Obsesses over clarity: writes things so anyone can execute them and removes ambiguity wherever it hides
  • Thinks in patterns: spots repeat issues fast, tags them consistently, and turns them into fixes
  • Balances customer-first with policy discipline: empathetic and flexible, but grounded in what we can promise and deliver
  • Collaborates without creating drag: brings solutions, not noise
  • Leads virtual training with a flexible schedule across time zones, and isn't afraid to take an escalation call when it counts
  • Owns the outcome with extreme ownership, with no micromanagement needed and always ten steps ahead

Compensation & Benefits

At Grüns, we're committed to providing a competitive total compensation package—grounded in market data that considers our size, stage, industry, and location. For this role, the base salary range is between $100,000 – $110,000 plus bonus depending on experience.

Beyond base salary, we offer competitive equity packages and a comprehensive set of benefits designed to support the well-being, growth, and balance of our team.

A bit about us...

At Grüns, we believe that foundational nutrition should be simple and convenient for everyone. We're dedicated to bringing comprehensive and real nutrition to you through our gummies, formulated from 60 nutrient-dense and whole-food ingredients. Simply enjoy a grab-and-go snack pack of gummies daily whenever fits best in your schedule and wherever life takes you.

Like you, we were disappointed. There’s an infinite number of “nutrition” companies, all focused on what’s best for them — not what’s best for you. Hundreds of products to sell you on, low-quality ingredients, and small nutrient doses. We’ve seen it all.

So we decided it was time to fix it. No more choking on and popping pills like a pharmacy. No more clean-up and disgust from gross powders. And no more cobbling together handfuls to dozens of supplements. Grüns is comprehensive nutrition, made convenient and delicious.

What we care about...

Be the Best: We hold ourselves, our teams, and our partners to an incredibly high standard - and we raise the bar constantly. "We've never done this before" isn't an excuse here. It's an invitation.

Own It: We act like our name is on the door. That means taking complete ownership of outcomes, collaborating deeply, working through roadblocks - not around them - and never waiting for someone else to solve the problem. Great owners are great partners.

Drive Impact, Urgently: We measure impact, not effort. We work smart and hard, move fast, and use every tool at our disposal - including AI - to focus our energy where it matters most.

Compensation & Perks:

For every role, we aim to have highly competitive compensation and opportunity for impact and career growth.

Everyone at Grüns works hard, but we believe in wellness and balance too. We have super strong benefits coverage -- for you and your family, generous PTO, free Grüns, and a few more perks centered around health and well-being that we can't wait to tell you about!

jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Stripe is beloved by developers for the simplicity of our APIs, the thoroughness of our documentation, and our focus on developer experience. The Technical Solutions Engineering (TSE) team is the glue that supports our developer-users and champions developer experience as being central to the overall experience of our users. TSE interacts directly with developer-users more than any other team at Stripe, so your role will have a significant impact on what Stripe is known for and values most. When we do our job well, developers all over the world are able to smoothly launch and grow their businesses on Stripe, whether they’re integrating payments for the first time or building complex financial systems.

What you’ll do

TSEs understand the fundamentals of programming incredibly well and eagerly jump in and familiarize themselves with others’ code. You will do a wide variety of things, including explaining technical concepts about Stripe’s products, build and debug integrations with developers, and produce/improve guides that help our users solve particular problems to be successful with Stripe. You will interact with developers of all skill levels through a variety of mediums, enabling them to be successful when using Stripe.

Early on, current team members will devote a large amount of time to teaching you and helping you get to a level of comfort and expertise with Stripe, its services, and how we interact with users. Later, we’d love for you to take on this role with others on the team and Stripes broadly, as teaching is a great way to learn and to reinforce what you know.

If you’re someone who enjoys working with all kinds of code, is a fast researcher, a strong writer, and enthusiastic about helping others build mission-critical products with Stripe, we want to hear from you!

Responsibilities

  • Communicate with a number of external developers and aid them in building their applications against Stripe’s infrastructure in a number of programming languages (including Java, Python, Ruby, PHP, Go, NodeJS, .NET, ReactJS, React Native, Swift, Objective-C, Kotlin, and Java for Android).
  • Unblock external developers with their thorniest integration challenges through a variety of support channels including email, ticketing software, internal issue trackers, community platforms (like StackOverflow), and real-time chat software (like Slack and Discord)
  • Develop and maintain internal and external documentation, examples, integration demos, and code-snippets that demonstrate usage patterns of the Stripe infrastructure.
  • Identify points of friction developers encounter and collaborate with engineering teams to make Stripe products better. Participate in a number of extended engineering teams’ regular planning sessions, design reviews, and development meetings.
  • Develop and maintain a suite of internal support tooling for TSE and Stripe Support more broadly e.g. a retrieval augmented generation LLM-based Copilot tool or the Invoice Explainer Admin tool.
  • Act as a developer advocate and educational resource internal to the organization by regularly assembling training for non-developers internal to the organization and responding in real-time to product integration questions.

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

This role is remote but requires candidates to be located in the Mountain or Pacific time zones.

Minimum requirements

  • At least 4 years of full-stack software development experience, with a proven track record of building web or mobile applications that deliver high-quality user experiences
  • Direct experience explaining technical concepts, and would be comfortable explaining how Stripe works to both technical and non-technical audiences
  • Understands how to write good, clean code in multiple programming languages, as well as how to read code that might not be quite as well written
  • Ability to help users during working hours in the region you are in. This may occasionally include providing weekend coverage for monitoring/supporting critical infrastructure, which TSEs are uniquely equipped to assist with given the team’s knowledge around Stripe’s products and active integrations. The team is largely remote, and we are very supportive of working arrangements that allow for family care and other needs to be met.

Preferred qualifications

  • Enjoys writing in a clear and quick manner
  • General software engineering skills are important to us, as we understand that new languages and frameworks can be learned if you understand the concepts
  • Experience teaching or coaching developers
  • Comfort working with a great deal of autonomy and limited supervision
  • Degree in Computer Science, Software/Computer Engineering, or a related analytical field of study
