What Your Experience Will Be:

As a Client Experience Manager at Slang AI, you’ll own the end-to-end customer journey for our SMB clients — from onboarding through long-term success and day-to-day support. You’ll guide customers through their initial rollout, transition seamlessly into serving as their long-term success manager, and directly manage the support inbox during business hours, where many of their most important interactions occur.
Because support volume is currently low (fewer than 60 inquiries per month across 1,500+ customers), this role offers the opportunity to both deliver excellent frontline support and help design how support scales as we grow. You’ll gain unique visibility into customer needs in real time while influencing the tools, processes, and standards that will shape support as the business expands.
This unique scope means you’ll be both a strategic advisor and a hands-on partner, ensuring customers launch smoothly, adopt key features, resolve challenges quickly, and realize the full value of Slang. By owning these critical touch points, you’ll have a large sphere of influence over customer outcomes, shaping retention, adoption, and satisfaction across a significant segment of the business.
In addition, you’ll play a key role in our digital customer success program — helping define and refine automated success sequences to ensure accuracy, consistency, and strong adoption results. This work ensures customers experience the same hospitality-first service at scale, while giving you a direct impact on how Slang drives measurable results for our clients.

Why You Belong Here & How You Will Grow:

At Slang, we believe success starts with great execution and great service. In this role, you’ll gain valuable experience managing full customer lifecycles and working with hospitality operators in a fast-paced environment. You’ll learn how to onboard, support, and grow a book of business with autonomy, while contributing to scalable processes that improve outcomes across the team. We offer training, feedback, and growth opportunities to help you level up in customer success, technical product fluency, and strategic account management.

What Success Looks Like

  • Driving Long-Term Success: You are responsible for the health and success of your assigned accounts. You ensure customers are seeing clear outcomes, meeting their goals, and staying on track for renewal.
  • Building Trusted Relationship: You build strong relationships with a range of customer stakeholders — from General Managers to Operations Leaders — and know how to tailor your approach depending on their needs.
  • Renewals & Retention: You own the renewal process and are accountable for maintaining and growing account revenue. You identify risks early, take action to resolve issues, and keep customers satisfied and committed.
  • Surfacing Growth Opportunity: You surface expansion opportunities (e.g. additional locations or use cases) and work with Sales to execute. You contribute to the team’s Net Revenue Retention (NRR) goal.
  • Feature Adoption & Product Fluency: You guide customers through product updates, encourage usage of key features, and tie adoption back to business outcomes. You’re expected to understand and explain Slang’s value.
  • Onboarding and Success Planning: You create simple account plans to track customer goals, key contacts, risks, and growth potential. You align internal teams around each plan to support execution.
  • Voice of the Customer: You escalate customer feedback internally and contribute insights that improve product and service. You partner with Product and Support to advocate for customer needs.
  • Hospitality-First Service: You respond quickly, handle challenges with professionalism, and make interactions easy for customers. You aim to create a positive experience in every conversation.

What You Will Bring

  • Customer Focus: You care about helping customers succeed. You’re responsive, thoughtful, and proactive.
  • Experience: 3+ years of experience in customer success, account management, or client-facing roles. Background in restaurants or hospitality tech is strongly preferred.
  • Business Acumen: You understand restaurant operations and how to align Slang’s value with business goals. You’re comfortable working with executives and frontline staff alike.
  • Communication: You’re clear and concise in both written and verbal communication. You know how to explain ideas, give updates, and lead customer conversations.
  • Ownership: You manage your book of business with attention to detail. You’re accountable for renewals, engagement, and outcomes.
  • Adaptability: You’re comfortable in a fast-changing environment and open to feedback. You handle ambiguity and know how to prioritize.
  • Preferred: Experience with restaurant operations, phone systems, or reservation platforms is a plus.

How Work Affects My Life:

As a Client Experience Manager for SMBs, you’ll directly contribute to the success of hospitality teams. Your work helps restaurant staff be more productive, improve guest service, and hit their business goals. In return, Slang supports you with competitive pay, benefits, and a culture that values performance and teamwork. You’ll have clear goals, a meaningful role, and the opportunity to grow.

Our Vision

Calling a business shouldn’t feel like a robot-hostage situation, where you’re forced to listen to horrible music and can't reach a human, while enduring a soulless voice uttering "I'm sorry I didn't quite get that" on repeat for eternity. (shudder) That’s why we started Slang.ai. We use the latest AI and audio wizardry to make transacting via voice so enjoyable it’s more human than human. By 2030, we will save businesses and consumers 1 billion minutes of precious time while transforming voice channels into the preferred mode of communication (it's faster and easier than text).
We have backgrounds building product at companies like Spotify, Buzzfeed, the New York Times, and OpenTable —shipping experiences that have reached hundreds of millions of users. Now, we’re using our backgrounds to start a new culture, one that puts product and human-centered design above all else while fostering constant learning and growth. Sound like something you’d like to be part of? Get on board.

Our Values

Overachiever Fever. We’re overachievers (we don’t know any other way)
Learner Fervor. We take every opportunity to learn (especially when it’s hard)
Humility Ability. We approach each other with curiosity and openness (know-it-alls not welcome!)
SMB MVP. We’re an expert member of our customers’ teams (we earn their trust)

jobs.description:
HexCoded is an AI video studio: you should be able to make anything you can imagine. We are a very small team building the tools that are reshaping how video, image and audio get made. Check out hexcoded.ai

What you'll actually work on

  • Make the content. Reels, shorts, posts, hooks, thumbnails, captions. Most of it made in HexCoded itself, posted in public.
  • Run our editors. We work with a bench of freelance video editors. You write the brief, pick the reference, chase the deadline, and send it back when it isn't right. Content nobody chases doesn't get made.
  • Fill the Discord. We have one. It's nearly empty. Getting people in there and keeping it alive is yours — inviting them, welcoming them by name, starting the conversation on the quiet days, and telling the rest of us what those people actually want from us.
  • Write the emails. All of them. The hello when someone signs up. The nudge that gets them to make their first ad. The note to people who drifted away. The announcement when we launch something. You write it, you send it.
  • Write the ads. You'll sit with the ad account, see which ads are doing well, and write the next batch. You won't control the budget. You'll be the one who knows why the winner won.
  • Watch the numbers. Views, saves, Discord joins, replies, signups. Not for a report. Because you can't get better at this without knowing which of your posts worked and which died.

What you'll bring

  • An account you've actually run. Yours, a friend's, a college club's, a page about something you love. Send us links and real numbers, including the posts that flopped.
  • Taste you can explain. Show you two thumbnails and you can say which one wins and why, in a sentence. "It just feels better" is where you start, not where you stop.
  • You already build things with AI. Not a chat tab you ask questions in. Actual work. You've had a model rename two hundred clips at once, pull a week of numbers into one place, write thirty versions of a caption so you could pick the best one, or make some small thing that saves you an hour every day. You'll do a lot of that here, including in Claude Code, which is Claude running on your computer where it can work on your files directly. You don't need to know it already. You do need to have used AI to save yourself real time, and be able to show us what you made.
  • Short, clear writing. Most of what you make is a few words a stranger reads once and judges us on.
  • You're properly online. You knew what happened on Instagram this week before anyone told you. You can name a format that died and say what killed it.

jobs.excerpt: Securing NVIDIA's EDA clusters is not a matter of deploying a standard security stack.
jobs.description:
Securing NVIDIA's EDA clusters is not a matter of deploying a standard security stack. The workloads are too large, too long-running, and too performance-sensitive for an off-the-shelf playbook to simply apply. That constraint is the job. You'll be an individual contributor on Infrastructure Security Engineering for EDA Clusters, the team that implements security controls across the compute, storage, and networking that NVIDIA's hardware engineers design silicon on - spanning on-prem data centers and multi-cloud. You will sit alongside the engineers who run these clusters 24x7, close enough to deploy a control, investigate a behavior, and change the running environment yourself.


This is hands-on build work, not control review. You'll decide where conventional tooling applies, where it actively cannot, and then engineer the alternative. If your depth is in large-scale compute, networking, or storage infrastructure at a hyperscaler, a security product company, or anywhere fleets and fabrics are the day job, and you've carried real accountability for the security properties of those systems, you're who we want to talk to. We don't expect fluency in every security product category. We expect you to own outcomes and pick up the remaining domain breadth fast. Security engineering here is engineering: code, instrumentation, and secure-by-default infrastructure - not tickets, exceptions, and spreadsheets.


What You'll Be Doing:

  • Build and operate security controls and telemetry for EDA compute, storage, and networking - design, ship to production, then own them.
  • Engineer around hard constraints. Protect multi-day, high-value compute jobs without degrading them. Where heavyweight in-node agents are not viable, build the workable answer instead.
  • Make the network and platform the control plane. Protection can't depend solely on what runs inside the node.
  • Instrument for detection. Collect and normalize security signals from the fleet into our SIEM, and build the detections and dashboards that turn it into something actionable. Log collection alone is not monitoring.
  • Investigate and respond. Chase down EDA-specific threats and exposure, and execute containment and remediation hands-on with infrastructure and service owners.
  • Automate enforcement and evidence. Infrastructure-as-code and policy-as-code so secure configuration is the default state, with compliance evidence produced as an engineering output rather than a manual exercise.
  • Run the lifecycle of the security technologies you own: selection, rollout, operation, and eventual replacement.
  • Work across boundaries. Partner directly with data center operations, IT storage and networking, network engineering, CSP teams, and NVIDIA's central security organization on shared outcomes.
  • Think like an adversary. Threat modeling and mitigation planning across network, storage, and compute.

What We Need To See:

  • 8+ years of hands-on infrastructure or infrastructure-security engineering across on-prem and cloud environments.
  • Strong Linux depth - you are comfortable at the system level, not just the console level.
  • Real experience operating or securing compute fleets at scale: provisioning, lifecycle, and the operational realities of long-running jobs.
  • Working networking expertise applied to large compute environments.
  • Programming/scripting fluency (Python, Go, or shell) used for automation, detection, and tooling you've shipped and maintained.
  • Solid foundations in access control, authentication, segmentation, encryption, and vulnerability lifecycle.
  • A track record of landing changes with partners who don't report to you.
  • Clear written and verbal communication - credible with individual engineers and with leadership.
  • A Bachelor's degree in a relevant engineering field or equivalent experience.

Ways To Stand Out from the Crowd:

  • Security or platform engineering inside EDA, HPC, or large research-cluster environments.
  • Breadth across security domains - IAM, EDR/XDR, CNAPP, CSPM, zero-trust architectures - or a demonstrated pattern of picking up new domains fast.
  • Built or operated infrastructure security capabilities at a hyperscaler or a security product company - you engineered detection and enforcement systems rather than deploying someone else's.
  • Experience with kernel- and fabric-level observability and enforcement - eBPF, in-line and out-of-band inspection, DPU/SmartNIC offload - as an alternative to heavyweight in-node agents.
  • Contributions to open-source security or infrastructure tooling.

Widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers, NVIDIA offers highly competitive salaries and a comprehensive benefits package. We have some of the most forward-thinking and talented people in the world working for us and, due to outstanding growth, our world-class engineering teams are growing fast. If you're a creative and autonomous engineer with real passion for technology, we want to hear from you.

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and the pay of employees in similar positions. The base salary range is 184,000 USD - 287,500 USD for Level 4, and 224,000 USD - 356,500 USD for Level 5.

Overview

LMI is seeking a Director of Mission Growth to lead growth strategy, marketing, and mission delivery expansion for our Robotics and Autonomous Systems (RAS) portfolio. This position will be responsible for shaping strategy across multiple defense markets, homeland security, and other Government agencies to position LMI's technology capabilities against leading autonomy, robotics, and unmanned systems initiatives. This role requires a senior growth leader who connects marketing, business development, customer engagement, and product positioning into one integrated plan that delivers capability to our mission partners.

The Director will work with RAS leadership, mission delivery teams, technical experts, product teams, and program managers to streamline growth plans across markets and connect customer missions with solutions spanning robotics, autonomous systems, mission software, artificial intelligence, data, systems integration, test and evaluation, training, procurement, and sustainment, including a growing portfolio of LMI proprietary products and platforms.

LMI is a new breed of digital solutions provider dedicated to accelerating government impact with innovation and speed. Investing in technology and prototypes ahead of need, LMI brings commercial-grade platforms and mission-ready AI to federal agencies at commercial speed.

Leveraging our mission-ready technology and solutions, proven expertise in federal deployment, and strategic relationships, we enhance outcomes for the government, efficiently and effectively. With a focus on agility and collaboration, LMI serves the defense, space, healthcare, and energy sectors—helping agencies navigate complexity and outpace change. Headquartered in Tysons, Virginia, LMI is committed to delivering impactful results that strengthen missions and drive lasting value.

This is a remote position that requires the ability to obtain a Secret security clearance. Periodic travel is required for customer engagements, industry events, demonstrations, capture activities, and meetings at government or LMI locations. Classified work must be performed in approved facilities.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute the RAS growth strategy, unifying marketing, business development, customer engagement, capture, and product positioning into one integrated plan spanning Special Operations, Joint, service, homeland security, and other Government agency markets.
  • Streamline growth plans across markets into a single portfolio roadmap that prioritizes pursuits, sequences investments, and accelerates delivery of technology capabilities to Government customers.
  • Align the RAS portfolio with the Department of War's leading autonomy, robotics, and unmanned systems initiatives, anticipating emerging requirements and positioning capabilities ahead of need.
  • Lead marketing and positioning for the RAS portfolio, including capability messaging, product campaigns, demonstrations, industry events, and thought leadership that differentiate LMI's ability to accredit, integrate, and operationalize autonomy for Government missions.
  • Build alignment among Government customers, operational users, program offices, acquisition organizations, industry partners, and LMI market leadership so growth priorities, investments, and delivery commitments stay synchronized.
  • Develop market intelligence and competitive assessments that inform market entry decisions, bid strategies, win themes, and discriminators tied to customer priorities and evaluation criteria.
  • Own the RAS opportunity pipeline, enforcing qualification discipline, leading pipeline and capture reviews, and providing award forecasts and growth reporting to RAS and corporate leadership.
  • Direct high priority captures from qualification through proposal submission and award transition, and shape responses to requests for information, white papers, capability statements, proposals, and oral presentations.
  • Grow the partner ecosystem by identifying teaming needs, assessing vendors and technology partners, and coordinating teaming strategies and agreements with LMI leadership and contracts personnel.
  • Partner with product and delivery teams to translate operator feedback and mission outcomes into product roadmaps, expansion of existing programs, and new offerings that extend mission impact.
  • Leverage rapid acquisition pathways, including Other Transaction agreements and Commercial Solutions Openings, to move capability to the mission at speed.
  • Maintain accurate opportunity records and engagement history in LMI's customer relationship management system, capture lessons from wins, losses, and customer feedback, and transition awarded work to delivery teams with documented commitments and expectations.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • Ability to obtain a Secret security clearance, with the ability to maintain the clearance throughout employment.

  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university is required.

  • Minimum of ten years of federal business development, capture, marketing, or growth strategy experience, including experience leading growth for a defense portfolio, account, or business unit.

  • Demonstrated record of growing a defense business through integrated strategy, marketing, pipeline development, and capture leadership, with measurable contributions to contract awards and program expansion.

  • Demonstrated experience aligning multiple markets, customers, and internal stakeholders around a unified growth plan, including prioritizing pursuits and investments across competing demands.

  • Working knowledge of federal acquisition processes, contract vehicles, task-order competitions, and rapid acquisition pathways, and the relationship among customer requirements, funding, solicitations, and award decisions.

  • Ability to work with technical experts and product teams to understand capabilities, identify customer value, and communicate solutions accurately in meetings, briefings, and written responses.

  • Strong writing, briefing, research, organization, and stakeholder coordination skills, with the ability to manage concurrent pursuits and deadlines.

  • Experience maintaining opportunity pipelines and capture documentation using customer relationship management systems and Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and collaboration tools.

  • Ability to work independently in a remote environment, lead through influence, protect sensitive business information, and travel periodically.

Desired Qualifications

  • Master's degree in business administration, engineering, national security, technology management, or a related discipline.
  • Experience pursuing Department of War opportunities, particularly those supporting Special Operations Forces, combatant commands, military services, or defense technology organizations.
  • Growth, business development, or capture experience involving robotics, autonomous or uncrewed systems, counter-unmanned systems, mission software, artificial intelligence, data, systems integration, test and evaluation, training, or sustainment.
  • Experience with rapid acquisition and innovation opportunities, including Other Transaction agreements, Small Business Innovation Research Phase III, Commercial Solutions Openings, or Broad Agency Announcements.
  • Experience marketing and growing proprietary products and platforms within a defense services or technology company, including product campaigns, demonstrations, and industry engagement.
  • Demonstrated contributions to federal contract awards, recompetes, or expansion of existing programs.
  • Formal capture or proposal training, or professional certification through the Association of Proposal Management Professionals.

  • Je hebt ervaring in Kubernetes-omgevingen, en het schrijven van Helm charts is een must.

Responsibilities

Peraton is seeking an experienced and detail-oriented Senior Cloud Administrator to support the DOI USGS Permitting Modernization and Cloud Infrastructure program on the WARP platform. In this fully remote hands-on role you will serve as the day-to-day operational owner of the AWS cloud infrastructure supporting a diverse development workforce of 50+ engineers, 20 business analysts, and Government personnel across fully separated development, testing, staging, and production environments. You will manage AWS Marketplace subscriptions, enforce Government-directed security controls, monitor environment health, and serve as the primary point of contact for AWS support escalations. Operating in a strict FedRAMP Moderate federal environment, you will ensure platform availability, access integrity, and security compliance playing a foundational role in the success of one of DOI's most significant technology modernization programs.

Peraton supports the U.S. Department of the Interior (DOI) and U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) in modernizing the federal permitting process through the Permitting Modernization and Cloud Infrastructure program. At the heart of this initiative is the WARP platform (Workflows, Authorizations, Registrations, and Permits), a cloud-native AWS environment purpose-built to streamline and accelerate how the federal government processes permits, authorizations, and registrations. The program leverages cutting-edge cloud infrastructure, AI-assisted decision support, and advanced data engineering to serve a large, distributed team of developers, business analysts, and Government stakeholders. Peraton's role spans the full lifecycle of cloud operations from provisioning and managing secure multi-environment AWS infrastructure and AI/ML services to delivering workforce training and certification, all within a rigorous federal compliance framework including FedRAMP, FISMA, and NIST security standards.

Work Location: Remote

What You Will Do:

  • Administer and maintain all AWS cloud environments (dev, test, staging, production) for the WARP permitting platform, ensuring availability, performance, and security at all times.
  • Manage AWS Marketplace subscriptions, including procurement, provisioning, renewal, and decommissioning of approved runtime subscriptions for permitting and development workloads.
  • Monitor environment health and performance using AWS CloudWatch and other observability tools; triage and remediate alerts, incidents, and service disruptions in a timely manner.
  • Manage AWS support tickets and coordinate with AWS technical teams to resolve platform-level issues, service limits, and infrastructure anomalies.
  • Control and manage consumption throttling for compute, storage, AI/ML, and data services to prevent budget overruns, in coordination with the FinOps Cloud Engineer.
  • Administer data operations: cross-AZ/cross-region data transfer, AWS KMS key management, CloudTrail audit logging, centralized S3 log archival, and AWS Backup configurations.
  • Manage Databricks cluster provisioning, storage, and networking within the DOI-designated environment.
  • Administer user access and personnel tracking for all contractor and Government personnel accessing DOI systems; immediately notify the COR upon any personnel departure or role change.
  • Execute and maintain required security agreements, non-disclosure agreements, and DOI Rules of Behavior documentation for all personnel with unsupervised USGS system access.
  • Assist in maintaining C&A documentation, contingency plans (per NIST SP 800-34), and security assessment support materials.
  • Perform all system administration duties within Government-designated environments exclusively; no Peraton-owned storage or systems used for Government data.
  • Complete mandatory annual DOI IT Security Awareness Training and maintain compliance with all applicable DOI, FISMA, and FedRAMP security policies.

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelors degree and 10 years professional experience or a Masters degree and 8 years professional experience or an Associates degree and 12 years professional experience; or a high school diploma/equivalent and 14 years’ professional experience.
  • U.S. Citizenship required; must have the ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust clearance.
  • Must perform all work within the United States; no international work permitted under this contract.
  • 5 plus years of hands-on system or cloud administration experience, with at least 3 years in AWS environments.
  • Demonstrated experience administering multi-environment AWS cloud platforms (dev/test/staging/prod) at enterprise or federal scale.
  • Proficiency with AWS core services: EC2, S3, Lambda, Fargate, ECS/EKS, VPC, AWS Backup.
  • Hands-on experience with implementing and enforcing IAM policies, SCPs, Service Quotas, and access governance in AWS Organizations.
  • Hands-on experience with AWS KMS, CloudTrail, CloudWatch, and centralized log archival to S3.
  • Experience managing AWS Marketplace subscriptions and procurement workflows.
  • Knowledge of Identity and Access Management (IAM) best practices, least-privilege principles, and federated identity management.
  • Understanding of ETL pipelines and data platform operations within cloud environments.
  • Familiarity with Databricks cluster administration, including compute, storage, and networking configuration.
  • Familiarity with AWS Organizations, tag policies, service quota management, and multi-account governance.
  • Familiarity with DOI security policies, incident reporting requirements, and C&A processes.
  • Familiarity with NIST SP 800-34 (contingency planning) and NIST SP 800-64 (SDLC security integration).
  • Ability to create and maintain system documentation, runbooks, contingency plans, and incident response records.
  • Prior experience working in or administering FedRAMP Moderate or higher cloud environments.
  • Experience managing AWS support relationships, escalating technical issues, and driving resolution with cloud vendors.
  • One or more of the following certifications (or able to obtain with 90 days):
  • AWS Certified CloudOps Engineer – Associate
  • AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate or Professional

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Prior experience on a DOI, USGS, or other Department of Interior program.
  • Experience administering Databricks workspaces in a federated, multi-team environment.
  • Experience with SIEM tools or centralized security monitoring platforms.
  • Experience with NIST SP 800-37 Risk Management Framework (RMF) processes.
  • Working knowledge of FISMA, FedRAMP, and NIST SP 800-53 security controls applicable to cloud platforms
  • Working knowledge of DOI IT Systems Contingency Plan Guide and DOI Computer Incident Response Guide.
  • Familiarity with Amazon Bedrock or LLM/AI platform administration.
  • Familiarity with Section 508 accessibility requirements and accessibility testing tools.
  • Background in supporting agile software development teams using GitLab or Atlassian toolsets (Jira, Confluence).

Peraton Overview

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world’s leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees do the can’t be done by solving the most daunting challenges facing our customers. Visit peraton.com to learn how we’re keeping people around the world safe and secure.

Target Salary Range

$104,000 - $166,000. This represents the typical salary range for this position. Salary is determined by various factors, including but not limited to, the scope and responsibilities of the position, the individual’s experience, education, knowledge, skills, and competencies, as well as geographic location and business and contract considerations. Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay.

You could be a great fit if...

  • You like taking a feature from an idea or requirement all the way through to production.

  • You care about building production-ready systems, not just getting code to work.

  • You have strong TypeScript fundamentals and enjoy working with both React and Node.js.

  • You naturally think about scalability, security, performance, and maintainability when building features.

  • You enjoy solving complex problems across the browser, API, database, and infrastructure layers.

  • You take ownership when something breaks and are comfortable digging into logs, metrics, and production evidence to find the root cause.

  • You enjoy improving engineering workflows, code quality, testing, CI/CD, and development practices.

  • You're excited by the opportunity to help build a product and technical foundation from an early stage.

  • 6+ years of professional software engineering experience, with substantial ownership of production systems.

  • 3+ years of advanced TypeScript development across both frontend and backend.

  • Strong understanding of TypeScript, including generics, discriminated unions, type narrowing, utility types, and strict compiler configuration.

  • Advanced React experience, including component architecture, hooks, server state management, form performance, and reusable UI patterns.

  • Experience building complex forms using React Hook Form or an equivalent library, with schema validation using Zod, Yup, or JSON Schema.

  • Strong Node.js and NestJS experience, including dependency injection, modular architecture, validation, guards, interceptors, and exception handling.

  • Strong understanding of REST API design, including resource modelling, pagination, filtering, versioning, idempotency, and consistent error handling.

  • Strong PostgreSQL knowledge, including relational modelling, constraints, transactions, indexes, and query optimisation.

  • Experience with Prisma ORM, including migrations and avoiding inefficient database query patterns.

  • Experience securing web applications using JWT or OAuth 2.0, RBAC, secure cookies, token rotation, and OWASP practices.

  • Experience writing automated tests using Jest and browser-level tests using Playwright.

  • Production experience with Docker and CI/CD pipelines.

  • Practical AWS experience across areas such as container deployment, managed databases, object storage, load balancing, IAM, configuration management, and observability.

  • Strong Git skills and experience working through pull requests and technical code reviews.

  • Ability to independently investigate and resolve issues across frontend, backend, database, and cloud infrastructure.

Bonus Points

  • Experience with Nx or another JavaScript monorepo build system.

  • Experience building multi-tenant SaaS products and implementing tenant-level data isolation.

  • Experience with performance optimisation and observability for distributed applications.

  • Experience working in a startup or 0→1 product environment.

  • Experience building products involving AI agents, AI workflows, or LLM-powered applications.

  • Experience working closely with Product teams to turn ambiguous requirements into technical solutions.

What Success Looks Like

  • Features are strongly typed from database and API contracts through to the React interface.

  • Authentication, authorisation, and tenant boundaries are enforced securely at the server level.

  • Database changes are supported by safe migrations, appropriate constraints, and thoughtful indexing.

  • Critical business workflows have meaningful automated test coverage.

  • Pull requests are clean, maintainable, and supported by clear technical reasoning.

  • Production issues can be traced through structured logs, metrics, and reproducible evidence.

  • Services can be deployed through automated, repeatable pipelines without manual configuration.

  • You take ownership of what you build and continuously improve the reliability and quality of the platform.

You probably shouldn't apply if...

  • You prefer working exclusively on either frontend or backend.

  • You need detailed instructions before making technical decisions.

  • You see engineering as simply writing code against predefined tickets.

  • You're uncomfortable working in an environment where requirements and priorities evolve quickly.

  • You don't enjoy debugging problems that span multiple layers of the technology stack.

jobs.excerpt: Talent Acquisition Specialist SnapshotCurvion Blue is looking for a Talent Acquisition Specialist who knows how to find, assess, and attract high-performing sales talent.
jobs.description:
Talent Acquisition Specialist Snapshot

Curvion Blue is looking for a Talent Acquisition Specialist who knows how to find, assess, and attract high-performing sales talent.

This isn't a traditional HR recruiting role where you're posting jobs, waiting for applications, and hoping the right person wanders into the funnel.

You're going to be responsible for building and managing talent pipelines for sales roles across our business, with a heavy focus on identifying A-Players who can perform in high-ticket sales environments.

The ideal candidate has experience in Talent Acquisition or recruiting and understands how to source, qualify, interview, and move candidates through a high-volume hiring process.

Bonus points if you've actually sold before. Extra bonus points if you've sold high-ticket.

We want someone who understands salespeople because they've been one, worked closely with them, or recruited them extensively.

Position Overview

As a Talent Acquisition Specialist, you will own recruiting across Curvion Blue's sales organization and help us continuously build a bench of exceptional talent.

You'll work closely with leadership to understand what "great" looks like for each role, then take that profile into the market and find the people who match it.

This is a hands-on recruiting role for someone who enjoys sourcing, talking to candidates, assessing talent, and moving quickly.

You will be responsible for the full recruiting lifecycle, including sourcing, candidate outreach, screening, interview coordination, candidate evaluation, pipeline management, and offer management.

More importantly, you'll become an expert in identifying the difference between someone who sounds like a great salesperson and someone who can actually perform.

Your Core Responsibilities

Talent Sourcing

  • Build proactive talent pipelines for closers, setters, sales leaders, and other revenue-generating roles.

  • Source candidates through LinkedIn, job boards, referrals, communities, databases, and creative outbound strategies.

  • Develop targeted sourcing strategies based on role requirements and candidate profiles.

  • Continuously build talent pools rather than starting from zero every time a role opens.

Candidate Qualification

  • Conduct recruiter screens to evaluate experience, communication, motivation, sales ability, and overall fit.

  • Identify candidates with demonstrated performance rather than relying solely on resume keywords.

  • Assess candidates against defined scorecards and role-specific success profiles.

  • Understand sales metrics, quotas, KPIs, close rates, lead flow, revenue, and other performance indicators.

  • Identify red flags and know when to move a candidate forward versus cut them from the process.

Sales Talent Acquisition

  • Become deeply familiar with high-ticket sales roles and the characteristics of top-performing setters, closers, sales directors, and sales leaders.

  • Understand the difference between legitimate sales experience and resume fluff.

  • Build relationships with high-performing sales professionals and maintain a warm talent network.

  • Help Curvion Blue become known as a destination for high-performing sales talent.

Candidate Experience

  • Own candidate communication throughout the recruiting process.

  • Keep candidates engaged, informed, and moving through each stage.

  • Represent Curvion Blue professionally and enthusiastically.

  • Create a candidate experience that reflects the level of talent we want to attract.

Recruiting Operations

  • Maintain accurate candidate data and pipeline stages in our ATS.

  • Track recruiting metrics including pipeline volume, conversion rates, time-to-fill, source performance, and quality of hire.

  • Coordinate interviews, skills assessments, roleplays, and other evaluation stages.

  • Partner with hiring managers to continuously improve the recruiting process.

  • Identify bottlenecks and recommend ways to improve recruiting efficiency.

Hiring & Onboarding Partnership

  • Support offer creation and candidate closing.

  • Help ensure strong candidates remain engaged through acceptance and start date.

  • Partner with the team to identify early indicators of successful hires.

  • Track quality of hire and use performance data to improve future recruiting decisions.

You SHOULD Apply If

  • You have 1+ years of Talent Acquisition, recruiting, or full-cycle recruiting experience.

  • You have experience recruiting salespeople, preferably revenue-generating roles.

  • You know how to source candidates rather than relying exclusively on inbound applicants.

  • You're comfortable conducting candidate screens and making recommendations to hiring managers.

  • You can quickly identify whether someone's experience actually matches what they're claiming.

  • You are highly comfortable talking to salespeople.

  • You understand performance-driven environments and aren't intimidated by metrics.

  • You can manage multiple open roles without losing track of candidates or details.

  • You're organized, responsive, and operationally strong.

  • You're comfortable working in an environment where priorities can move quickly.

  • You can communicate professionally with candidates at every level.

  • You're proactive. If you see a recruiting problem, your instinct is to solve it rather than wait for someone to tell you what to do.

BIG BONUS POINTS

  • You have past sales experience.

  • You have high-ticket sales experience.

  • You've been a setter, closer, AE, sales manager, or sales leader.

  • You've recruited high-ticket closers or setters before.

  • You've worked in coaching, consulting, SaaS, agency, or other performance-driven sales environments.

  • You understand sales compensation structures and can speak intelligently about earning potential with candidates.

  • You have an established network of sales talent.

  • You've recruited for remote sales organizations.

You SHOULD NOT Apply If

  • You only want to work inbound applications.

  • You don't enjoy outbound sourcing.

  • You need every step of your day mapped out for you.

  • You don't like metrics or performance accountability.

  • You're uncomfortable making judgment calls on candidates.

  • You struggle to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.

  • You view recruiting as simply scheduling interviews and forwarding resumes.

  • You don't enjoy talking to people.

  • You're looking for a slow-moving corporate environment with six approval layers before anything gets done.

  • You have never recruited before and are looking for your first opportunity in Talent Acquisition.

Long-Term

You become one of the people Curvion Blue relies on to answer:

"We need five great salespeople. Where are they?"

And your answer is:

"Already working on it."

The Person We're Looking For

We're not looking for someone who simply wants to "work in HR."

We're looking for a talent hunter.

Someone who enjoys the chase.

Someone who can look at a LinkedIn profile and immediately start thinking:

"This person might be good. Let me find out."

You should enjoy talking to people, asking good questions, spotting potential, and figuring out what makes someone tick.

You should be competitive enough to care about winning the search, analytical enough to care about hiring quality, and organized enough to keep the machine running.

If you've sold before, you'll probably have a natural advantage here because you already understand how to build rapport, overcome objections, create urgency, and influence decisions.

If you've sold high-ticket, even better. You already understand the world our candidates operate in.

At Curvion Blue, we're building revenue engines for our clients. That requires exceptional people.

Your job is to help us find them.

Schedule:

  • Monday to Friday

  • 9AM - 6 PM (specific to your time zone)

Compensation Range: $50K - $80K

jobs.excerpt: Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!
jobs.description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times.

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies.

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

What the job actually feels like

This is a build job.

When you join, BLP has no US pipeline, no US case studies, and no local playbook. It’s not the well-oiled machine with sophisticated processes for everything. What you get instead: an experienced Senior Account Executive sitting next to you, a country manager owning the strategy, a direct reporting line to the VP of Business Development in Europe and a strong DACH SDR team willing to support. You get a winning product and a market nobody here has sold into yet. All of that comes with strong support from the Switzerland HQ.

Your first job is to work out who buys, why, and what makes them pick up the phone. You will hear no far more often than yes. The yes is a 30-minute discovery call with a CFO, COO, or Head of Finance at a large US manufacturer or industrial business, where you run the meeting, present the value, and map the stakeholders live.

If you want a finished machine to plug into, this is the wrong role. If you want to help build the machine, read on.

About the role

As our SDR in Boston, you will own outreach into US enterprise accounts. You will prospect and open relationships with Finance and Procurement leaders (CFO, COO, Head of Shared Services, Process Excellence, AP) and generate qualified opportunities for our agentic AI platform automating Purchase-to-Pay and Order-to-Cash. Don’t expect inbounds to carry you from day one.

You are one of the first commercial hires on the ground in a new market. You prospect, you run the connect calls, and you help write the playbook the next US hires will use. You report directly to the VP of Business Development for now, work day to day with the US Account Executive as a tag-team, and lean on the Team in Europe for what already works.

You will monitor the US market with regards to procurement and finance processes, ERP transformation announcements and buying triggers, and turn what you learn into better targeting. We need you to flag what is not working early and bring it to the team, so we fix the approach fast instead of grinding on a broken one.

You won’t be the only commercial hire on the ground, as a team of BDRs and a BDR manager are being hired.

Tech stack

You will work with a sharp outbound stack: HubSpot as our CRM and source of truth, Clay for enrichment and signal-based prospecting, Claude for AI assisted tasks and research, and LinkMatch to keep LinkedIn and HubSpot in sync without manual logging. That said, the work has a strong outbound and calling focus. You will help decide what to add as the motion matures.

What you'll do

  • Take ownership of strategic outreach into enterprise accounts through cold calls and personalized messages, engaging CFO, CIO, CPO and COO stakeholders.

  • Craft tailored value propositions by understanding the specific pain points of stakeholders across Finance, Procurement, Operations and IT in Purchase-to-Pay and Order-to-Cash processes.

  • Prospect large accounts and build multi-threaded stakeholder maps across Finance, Procurement, Operations, IT and the executive sponsor.

  • Run and present in 30-minute discovery calls with C-level stakeholders. You own the meeting, not just the booking.

  • Position blp against point tools and fragmented stacks (OCR, IDP, workflow automation, RPA, copilots) with an end-to-end, exceptions-first narrative.

  • Stay ahead of the market by continuously updating your commercial knowledge, analyzing procurement and finance processes, and tracking industry trends in agentic AI and ERP automation.

  • Prioritize complex tasks with clients and identify potential bottlenecks to keep things moving forward.

  • Own a pipeline generation target and report proactively on progress, risks, and what you need from the organization.

We're excited about you because

  • You have roughly 1 to 2+ years in a B2B SaaS SDR or BDR role, most of it outbound, and you have built or helped build an outbound motion rather than only working an established one.

  • You know the US market and can navigate US enterprise buyers, ideally with experience selling into manufacturing, industrial, or finance and procurement buyers,

  • You communicate clearly, concisely, and persuasively, and adapt your style to a CFO, CIO, CPO or COO conversation.

  • You can run a discovery call with a senior stakeholder: you hold the room, communicate clearly, adapt to a CFO or a Head of Procurement, and understand the buying center.

  • You are comfortable with ambiguity. No inbound, no case studies, no script on day one does not rattle you, it interests you. You see opportunity.

  • You enjoy problem-solving and have a natural curiosity that drives you to find creative solutions.

  • You are looking for a role that comes with key responsibility beyond the typical SDR scope.

  • You take ownership, ask for help when you are stuck, act on feedback, and pass on what you learn to the people who join after you.

Bonus points

  • You have been the first SDR in a new market, or helped stand up a new territory.

  • You know the ERP domain, or have sold Finance, Procurement, or industrial software and are familiar with P2P/O2C processes.

  • You are familiar with HubSpot as a CRM and use AI daily to make you more productive.

What you'll get

  • US office. This role is based in our Boston office.

  • High earning potential. Uncapped commission and expected 6-figure package.

  • Equal OTEs. As we share the same incentives, you'll be comped as the Account Executives.

  • Training and development. There is onboarding material that trains you on our product, you get support from the EMEA SDR team and direct reporting line to the VP Business Development.

  • Aligned incentives with the AE team. You share the same on-target earnings structure as our Account Executives, because you share the same goal. Your work is treated as revenue generation, not lead handoff.

  • A stake in what you build. Long-term participation in the company's success, with details discussed openly during the process.

  • 25 days of paid vacation. European-standard time off, well above the US norm, because sustained performance depends on it.

  • Benefits. Plans around Medical, Dental, Vision, & Life and disability

  • Growth and autonomy. Build your own success path in a rapidly scaling, internationally expanding company.

  • Exceptional colleagues. Ambitious, collaborative people from strong academic and professional backgrounds who push each other toward excellence.

Learn more about blp and our values at .

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, ancestry, marital status, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

And more—we’re growing and evolving, so tell us what matters most to you!

About the Role

Clarity Pediatrics is seeking a licensed Group Therapist to join our remote, multidisciplinary behavioral health team. In this specialized role, you will exclusively facilitate virtual, evidence-based psychoeducational groups for parents and caregivers of children with behavioral health needs, primarily ADHD and anxiety.

Our parent groups equip caregivers with practical, evidence-based strategies they can use at home to support their child and strengthen family functioning. You’ll guide families through structured curricula, create an engaging and supportive group environment, and help parents translate what they learn into meaningful change between sessions.

You do not need to be an expert in every Clarity curriculum when you join. We provide training, structured materials, and ongoing clinical support to help you develop expertise in the programs you facilitate.

This is a great fit for a clinician who loves working with parents, enjoys the energy and impact of group-based care, and is excited by the opportunity to develop deep expertise in evidence-based parent interventions.

What You’ll Own

  • Facilitate structured, virtual treatment groups for parents and caregivers, including evidence-based programs supporting families of children with ADHD and anxiety

  • Help parents understand and apply evidence-based behavioral health strategies to challenges they are experiencing at home

  • Manage group dynamics effectively, including balancing participation, redirecting discussion, and maintaining appropriate boundaries and scope

  • Complete timely, accurate clinical documentation associated with group sessions

  • Collaborate with Clarity’s behavioral health and multidisciplinary teams when families need additional clinical support or a different level of care

  • Participate in training, consultation, and ongoing quality improvement to strengthen Clarity’s group-based care model

  • Maintain reliable availability for recurring group cohorts and provide continuity for families throughout the duration of a group program

About You

  • You’re a licensed mental health professional with either:

    • A master’s degree in a relevant behavioral health field and active licensure as an LMFT, LCSW, or LPCC; or

    • A doctoral degree in psychology (PhD or PsyD) with active licensure as a psychologist

  • You’re currently licensed in Texas and open to getting licensed in other states (we’ll support you with that!)

  • You're passionate about providing excellent care to kids and families

  • You have experience working with parents and caregivers of children and adolescents and are comfortable supporting families around behavioral, emotional, or developmental concerns

  • You have experience delivering evidence-based parent-focused interventions via telehealth

  • You have experience working with children and families impacted by ADHD, anxiety, or related behavioral health concerns.

  • You have experience facilitating groups, classes, workshops, or other structured clinical or psychoeducational programming.

  • You’re a strong facilitator who can communicate clinical concepts clearly, keep a group engaged, and navigate different personalities and levels of participation

jobs.excerpt: Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!
jobs.description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times.

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies.

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

What the job actually feels like

This is a build job.

When you join, BLP has no UK pipeline, no UK case studies, and no local playbook. It’s not the well-oiled machine with sophisticated processes for everything. What you get instead: an experienced Account Executive sitting next to you, a reporting line to the VP of Business Development and a strong DACH SDR team behind you. You get a winning product and a market nobody here has sold into yet. All of that comes with strong support from the Switzerland HQ.

Your first job is to work out who buys, why, and what makes them pick up the phone. You will hear no far more often than yes. The yes is a 30-minute discovery call with a CFO, COO, or Head of Finance at a large UK manufacturer or industrial business, where you run the meeting, present the value, and map the stakeholders live.

If you want a finished machine to plug into, this is the wrong role. If you want to help build the machine, read on.

About the role

As our Founding SDR in London, you own outbound into UK enterprise accounts. You will prospect and open relationships with Finance and Procurement leaders (CFO, COO, Head of Shared Services, Process Excellence, AP) and generate qualified opportunities for our agentic AI platform automating Purchase-to-Pay and Order-to-Cash. Don’t expect inbounds to carry you from day one.

You are one of the first commercial hires on the ground in a new market. You prospect, you run the connect calls, and you help write the playbook the next UK hires will use. You report directly to the VP of Business Development for now, work day to day with the UK Account Executive as a tag-team, and lean on the DACH SDR team for what already works.

You will monitor the UK market with regards to procurement and finance processes, ERP transformation announcements and buying triggers, and turn what you learn into better targeting. We need you to flag what is not working early and bring it to the team, so we fix the approach fast instead of grinding on a broken one.

Once the UK team reaches critical mass and shows initial success, we hire a local team lead (internally or externally).

Tech stack

You will work with a sharp outbound stack: HubSpot as our CRM and source of truth, Clay for enrichment and signal-based prospecting, Claude for AI assisted tasks and research, and LinkMatch to keep LinkedIn and HubSpot in sync without manual logging. That said, the work has a strong outbound and calling focus. You will help decide what to add as the motion matures.

We're excited about you because

  • You have roughly 2 to 5 years of experience in a B2B SaaS SDR or BDR role, most of it outbound, and you have built or helped build an outbound motion rather than only working an established one.

  • You know the UK market and can navigate UK enterprise buyers, ideally with experience selling to Finance, Procurement, or Operations.

  • You can run a discovery call with a senior stakeholder: you hold the room, communicate clearly, adapt to a CFO or a Head of Procurement, and understand the buying center.

  • You are comfortable with ambiguity. No inbound, no case studies, no script on day one does not rattle you, it interests you. You see opportunity.

  • You enjoy problem-solving and have a natural curiosity that drives you to find creative solutions.

  • You are looking for a role that comes with key responsibility beyond the typical SDR scope.

  • You take ownership, ask for help when you are stuck, act on feedback, and pass on what you learn to the people who join after you.

Bonus points

  • You have been a founding or first SDR in a new market, or helped stand up a new territory.

  • You know the ERP domain, or have sold Finance, Procurement, or industrial software and are familiar with P2P/O2C processes.

  • You are familiar with HubSpot as a CRM and Clay.

  • You speak another European language.

What you'll get

  • London Office. This role is based in our London office, You will spend regular time with your DACH peers in our HQ in Zurich and are invited over for onboarding.

  • Onboarding built for a founding rep. There is onboarding material that trains you on our product, you get a buddy from the DACH SDR team and direct support from the VP Business Development.

  • High earning potential. Uncapped commission and potential for a 6-figure package.

  • Equal OTEs. As we share the same incentives, you'll be comped as the Account Executives.

  • Opportunities to grow. You're controlling your personal development and career trajectory in a rapidly growing, internationally expanding startup.

  • Exceptional colleagues. You'll be growing alongside individuals from exceptional academic backgrounds and careers.

Learn more about blp and our values at .

About Company:
Arthan is a social enterprise focused on talent and leadership in the social impact sector. We work with NGOs, foundations, impact funds, and social enterprises across India and Asia to help them hire the right people and build stronger, more inclusive organisations. Our work spans executive search, talent consulting, thought leadership, and ecosystem building.

We are not just a placement firm — we're building the talent and leadership infrastructure of the social impact sector. That means identifying gaps, connecting practitioners across networks, convening sector actors, and strengthening how organisations approach talent and leadership development, particularly around gender equity and inclusion as well as building the capacity of the impact ecosystem through our thought leadership work in terms of research and knowledge dissemination through convenings and ecosystem engagements.

The Role:

This is a strategic business development and relationship management role operating at the heart of Arthan's growth and ecosystem-building work. You'll own a complex portfolio of institutional funder relationships, partnership conversations, and strategic ecosystem engagement. The work is high-stakes: institutional funders, sector networks, and strategic partners expect continuity, sophistication, and speed.

You'll work substantively, not administratively. This means authoring concept notes and proposals, leading initial partner discussions, conducting funder meetings, and representing Arthan's strategy with credibility. You'll need deep enough understanding of the landscape and the work to act independently, make judgment calls, and engage strategically when senior leadership isn't in the room.

Critically, this role is heavily tilted toward ecosystem building. Beyond managing current funder relationships, you'll spend significant time ideating on new partnerships, identifying collaboration opportunities, and actively working to strengthen the talent and leadership ecosystem in the social impact sector. You'll need to think strategically about who should be at the table, what partnerships could unlock sector-wide change, and how to bring people together around shared challenges. This is not a transactional role — it's about architecting relationships and collaborations that create systemic value.

The environment is fast-paced and multithreaded. You'll be holding multiple complex conversations at once, tracking timelines and commitments with precision, and delivering high-quality materials under pressure. This role demands someone who thrives in ambiguity, owns outcomes end-to-end, and sees relationship management and ecosystem building as strategic functions, not support functions.

What You'll Do:

  • Build and deepen relationships with institutional funders, strategic partners, and ecosystem players across the social impact sector
  • Ideate on new partnerships and collaboration opportunities — identifying who should be engaged, what aligned initiatives exist, and how to create value through partnership
  • Monitor the sector landscape and proactively flag emerging opportunities, partnerships, collaboration points, and funder priorities
  • Own all active business development conversations — tracking timelines, deliverables, decision points, and next steps with precision
  • Lead initial outreach to prospective partners and conduct substantive first-level relationship building with credibility
  • Draft concept notes, proposals, strategy briefs, and funder materials — high-quality, strategic work on tight deadlines
  • Prepare comprehensive briefs and talking points ahead of key meetings — capturing funder context, priorities, relationship history, and strategic considerations
  • Manage funder relationship continuity — understanding what drives each funder, tracking pending materials and responses, flagging delays, and maintaining momentum
  • Identify and pursue ecosystem-strengthening initiatives — collaborations, convenings, research, or networks that advance Arthan's mission and the broader sector
  • Keep all documentation clean and findable — meeting notes, opportunity trackers, decision logs, commitments, and relationship intelligence
  • Represent Arthan credibly in meetings and conversations — articulating strategy, communicating updates, and advancing relationships independently

Who We're Looking For:

If you are someone who thrives in this kind of role, you will have:

Essential

  • 5–10 years of professional experience, with at least 3 years in the development or social impact sector (NGOs, philanthropy, social enterprise, impact investing, or related fields)
  • Deep knowledge of the funder landscape — you understand different funder types, how they evaluate opportunities, what drives their decision-making, and how to engage them strategically
  • Existing networks and relationships in the social impact sector — funders, NGOs, social enterprises, and influencers who know you, respect your judgment, and value your perspective
  • Proven ability to write high-quality proposals, concept notes, and strategic documents — and to deliver them on tight deadlines without sacrificing quality
  • Strategic thinking and independent judgment — you take direction and run with it. You don't wait to be told twice, and you make smart calls in the moment
  • Ecosystem thinking — you understand systems, see potential partnerships and connections others miss, and can ideate on how disparate actors might work together to create greater impact
  • Excellent communication across written and spoken channels — you articulate complex ideas clearly, you hold your own in high-stakes conversations, and your writing is purposeful and compelling
  • Experience working directly with senior leaders or founders on business development and strategic partnerships
  • Background in talent, leadership development, gender equity, or organisational strengthening
  • Track record of convening, coalition-building, or ecosystem development work
  • Comfort navigating cross-cultural, cross-sector, and complex organisational ecosystems

Highly Valuable

We're a venture-backed startup that's raised over $28M from top-tier investors including Khosla Ventures (first investor in OpenAI, GitLab, Stripe, and DoorDash), and we're in a hyper-growth phase looking for motivated people to join our team. Our headquarters are in San Francisco (Salesforce Tower), but our team is distributed around the globe with a remote-first culture.

We give AI Cloud providers and AI factories a hyperscaler-like experience on their own GPU infrastructure. Our platform runs the full stack an operator needs, from bare metal provisioning and node lifecycle management up through managed Kubernetes, Slurm, Ray, and inference clusters, so they can turn raw GPUs into cluster products they can sell in days instead of spending 12+ months building it themselves. Today we power over 100,000 GPUs and 1 million CPUs across 50+ AI clouds and Fortune 500 companies, backed by a team of 40+ infrastructure engineers who build alongside our customers rather than just shipping them software.

We're the company behind vCluster, the open source technology for tenant isolation on Kubernetes, with 11,000+ GitHub stars and 40M+ tenant clusters created since 2021. Open source is part of our DNA. At KubeCon North America 2025, we launched our Infrastructure Tenancy Platform for AI, a Kubernetes-native framework built for running AI, ML, and GPU-intensive workloads anywhere, with an NVIDIA-validated reference architecture for DGX systems.

  • Workplace Flexibility: We’re very flexible about where you work. We know things can change in life and we’re happy to adjust the work environment for you along the way.

Culture & Values

At vCluster Labs, we value and stand for:

  1. Make it Happen: We have a relentless bias for action and the grit to push through obstacles. We do whatever it takes to figure it out, put in the work, and ruthlessly prioritize the actions that drive measurable impact for the business.

  2. Own the Outcome: We understand that our responsibility doesn't end when a task is checked off; it ends when the value is delivered. We connect our daily individual actions to the broader success of the company and our customers.

  3. Create Wow: We measure success by the experience we generate, both inside and outside the company. For our customers, this means impressive speed and intuitive experiences. For our team, this means going the extra mile to support one another and to continuously drive each other to new heights.

  4. Open Source, Open Mind: We are actively contributing to and maintaining open-source projects. Internally, we foster meritocracy — the strongest ideas win, no matter who or where they come from.

  5. Build Tomorrow’s Standards, Intentionally: We don't just ship software; we define the state-of-the-art of tomorrow. We are fearless in tearing down old approaches to build something better, but we are disciplined in how we do it because we know our users rely on our technology to run mission-critical infrastructure platforms.

Higharc is a VC-backed startup that is changing how new homes are designed and built. Join a founding team who’ve shipped products for Autodesk, Electronic Arts, Nike, and Apple. You'll help set technical direction as much as you write code, and you'll be comfortable with priorities shifting as the team finds its footing.

It's primarily an individual-contributor seat with room to grow into a tech lead. You don't need to be a career structural engineer, but structural or mechanical engineering experience is a real asset as you'll be the person who understands how framing and structural systems actually work and can turn that into software.

Expect to:

  • Design and implement the algorithms and systems behind framing and structural analysis, from early prototypes to a shippable MVP.

  • Use AI-assisted workflows to build quickly while owning the correctness, maintainability, and behavior of everything you ship.

  • Partner with product, customer success, and other engineers to define expected behavior, surface gaps, and keep customers happy.

  • Bring structural engineering judgment to the team, translating how framing and structural systems work into robust software.

  • Write tests that hold up against the worst corner cases.

  • Help shape a new team's technical direction and mentor others as it grows.

  • Navigate ambiguity as scope and priorities evolve on an emerging team.

About You

You prioritize working software over perfection. You like to ship, get user feedback, and iterate, and you're happy to dig deep into a codebase to contribute effectively to it. You're hands-on but keep the bigger strategic picture in view, and you're energized by building something new where the path isn't fully mapped yet. A genuine interest in homebuilding, construction, or home design is a plus, because you'll be helping elevate an entire industry.

You have:

  • 3–5 years of professional software engineering experience, ideally in TypeScript.

  • Structural or mechanical engineering experience, whether academic or professional.

  • Familiarity with computational geometry and mathematical modeling.

  • Professional fluency with modern development tools, including AI-assisted workflows, paired with clear ownership of the correctness and maintainability of the code you produce.

  • Comfort operating in ambiguity on a new and emerging team.

  • The ability to communicate tradeoffs, delivery timelines, and decisions clearly within a dynamic organization.

A major plus if you also bring:

  • Experience building framing, structural analysis, or CAD/CAM tooling.

  • A background moving between engineering stacks — many strong engineers in this space come from C# or Python, and picking up TypeScript and React is expected, not a barrier.

Working at Higharc

Remote work and travel: Our company is entirely remote, and has been since we were founded in 2018. Remote work means more time with family, less time commuting, and the flexibility to blend work and life. We value in-person collaboration and asynchronous deep-work time, which is why we schedule regular team meet-ups in our hubs across the US and, depending on the role, prioritize hiring in those hubs. If your role requires frequent travel beyond pre-scheduled team meet ups, we will represent that to the best of our ability as early as possible in the interview process.

Compensation and benefits: Higharc offers competitive salaries with significant equity, in a fast-growing, well-funded company. We provide comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, with flexible PTO, and meaningful maternity/paternity leave to all U.S based employees that are full-time. You'll also have access to other big-company benefits such like short and long-term disability plans and a 401K. We also provide a stipend to create the ideal home office and support ongoing L&D.
