About Abridge

Abridge was founded in 2018 with the mission of powering deeper understanding in healthcare. Our AI-powered platform was purpose-built for medical conversations, improving clinical documentation efficiencies while enabling clinicians to focus on what matters most—their patients.

Our enterprise-grade technology transforms patient-clinician conversations into structured clinical notes in real-time, with deep EMR integrations. Powered by Linked Evidence and our purpose-built, auditable AI, we are the only company that maps AI-generated summaries to ground truth, helping providers quickly trust and verify the output. As pioneers in generative AI for healthcare, we are setting the industry standards for the responsible deployment of AI across health systems.

We are a growing team of practicing MDs, AI scientists, PhDs, creatives, technologists, and engineers working together to empower people and make care make more sense. We have offices located in the Mission District in San Francisco, the SoHo neighborhood of New York, and East Liberty in Pittsburgh.

The Role

We're hiring a Staff Growth Marketer to build and own our product-led growth motion: the engine that turns clinicians who hear about Abridge into clinicians who use it every day, and turns that usage into expansion.

This is a senior individual contributor role with a heavy focus on PLG. You'll run point on all paid marketing (paid social, Google, programmatic, and OOH) and own the paid budget. You'll be the subject-matter expert for PLG across Marketing, setting direction for how we acquire, activate, and retain end users, partnering closely with Product, Data, and Sales to connect bottoms-up adoption to enterprise pipeline. You'll also be the go-to advisor for growth for the broader marketing team, coaching across enterprise demand, lifecycle, and expansion. We're looking for someone who can design the strategy, run the experiments, and raise the bar for everyone around them.

What You’ll Do

  • Define the PLG roadmap and connect it to every growth motion. Translate company goals into a prioritized plan for end-user acquisition, activation, engagement, and expansion, and align it with Product, Sales, and RevOps.

  • Own the end-user funnel. Map the clinician journey from first touch to habitual use. Identify the biggest drop-offs and build programs that move them: onboarding, in-product prompts, lifecycle email, and referral loops.

  • Run a high-velocity experimentation program. Set the hypothesis backlog, test design standards, and readout cadence. Ship tests across web, product surfaces, paid, and lifecycle, and scale what works.

  • Own paid marketing and the paid budget. Run point on all paid activity across paid social, Google, programmatic, and OOH. Set channel mix and budget allocation, manage platform and agency partners, and work with Product Marketing, Creative, Events, and Sales to plan, launch, and optimize campaigns against adoption and pipeline targets.

  • Connect bottoms-up adoption to enterprise pipeline. Partner with Sales and RevOps to define product-qualified signals, route them to the right teams, and show how usage drives expansion within health systems.

  • Build the measurement foundation for PLG. In partnership with Data Science and GTM Tech, define activation and retention metrics, attribution for product-led paths, and the dashboards the team runs on.

  • Pioneer new methods with AI. Build tools and workflows that speed up research, personalization, testing, and analysis, and coach the team to use them.

  • Advise on growth more broadly. Be the team's growth advisor beyond PLG. Coach marketers on experimentation, funnel analysis, and channel strategy, pressure-test growth plans for demand, lifecycle, and campaigns, and set standards others adopt.

What You’ll Bring

  • 10+ years of growth marketing experience, with at least 4 years owning product-led growth at a high-growth software company; AI company experience preferred

  • A track record of moving activation, conversion, or retention metrics at scale, and the funnel math to show it

  • Deep experimentation skills: Experiment across channels and tactics to drive user acquisition and translate results into scalable playbooks

  • Hands-on experience running paid programs across paid social, search, programmatic, and OOH, including owning the budget and reporting on its return

  • Strong B2C instincts in a B2B setting: you know how to reach and activate end users, and how their adoption earns the economic buyer's attention

  • Comfort building internal tools and workflows with AI, and a habit of using it to work faster and better

  • Low ego, high standards: direct, collaborative, and focused on outcomes over credit

Bonus Points

  • Experience driving PLG in healthcare, or selling to clinicians and other professional end users

  • Background building a self-serve or freemium motion from zero to one

  • Hands-on experience with referral, community, or word-of-mouth loops that grew a user base efficiently

Must be willing to work from our SF or NYC office at least 3x per week

This position requires a commitment to a hybrid work model, with the expectation of coming into the office a minimum of (3) three times per week.

We value people who are eager to learn new things and recognize that great team members might not perfectly match a job description. If you’re interested in the role but aren’t sure whether or not you’re a good fit, we’d still like to hear from you.

Why Work at Abridge?

At Abridge, we’re transforming healthcare delivery experiences with generative AI, enabling clinicians and patients to connect in deeper, more meaningful ways. Our mission is clear: to power deeper understanding in healthcare. We’re driving real, lasting change, with millions of medical conversations processed each month.

Joining Abridge means stepping into a fast-paced, high-growth startup where your contributions truly make a difference. Our culture requires extreme ownership—every employee has the ability to (and is expected to) make an impact on our customers and our business.

Beyond individual impact, you will have the opportunity to work alongside a team of curious, high-achieving people in a supportive environment where success is shared, growth is constant, and feedback fuels progress. At Abridge, it’s not just what we do—it’s how we do it. Every decision is rooted in empathy, always prioritizing the needs of clinicians and patients.

We’re committed to supporting your growth, both professionally and personally. Whether it's flexible work hours, an inclusive culture, or ongoing learning opportunities, we are here to help you thrive and do the best work of your life.

If you are ready to make a meaningful impact alongside passionate people who care deeply about what they do, Abridge is the place for you.

How we take care of Abridgers:

  • Comprehensive Health Plans: Medical, Dental, and Vision coverage for all full-time employees and their families.

Ema is building the world’s first Universal AI Employee — a production-grade agentic AI platform that automates real enterprise workflows across HR, IT, Finance, and Operations.

Ema’s customers do not run demos. They replace mission-critical, manual business processes with agentic AI systems that operate across multiple SaaS tools, APIs, and human-in-the-loop workflows.

  • Customer trust

    • AI behavior (false positives / negatives)

    • Data quality

    • Platform configuration

  • Handling Sev-1 / Sev-2 customer specific incidents calmly under customer pressure

5.2 Debugging, Diagnosis & Sev 1/2 Issue Resolution

  • Debug agentic workflows end-to-end

    • Model behavior

  • Ensure support insights influence roadmap and quality improvement

5.7 Support Operations & Excellence

  • Raise the overall support bar at Ema

Technical & Diagnostic Strength

  • Excellent debugging instincts

  • Comfortable operating in ambiguous systems

Ownership & Reliability Mindset

  • Issues do not bounce — they get owned

jobs.excerpt: About the DepartmentDNDi is a collaborative, non-profit research and development organisation working to develop and improve access to treatments for neglected diseases.
jobs.description:
About the Department

DNDi is a collaborative, non-profit research and development organisation working to develop and improve access to treatments for neglected diseases. Alongside its research programmes, DNDi shares capacity with institutions in affected countries across clinical research, data, regulatory systems and treatment access.

DNDi is exploring how these capabilities can contribute to larger, country-led programmes addressing health security, climate-sensitive diseases and equitable access to health services and medical products. Such programmes may bring together partners with complementary expertise, with DNDi contributing a defined technical role. DNDi has already undertaken some country-interest mapping, mapped relevant instruments across several multilateral development banks, held initial exploratory discussions, and developed outlines of several potential programme propositions. The consultant will review, test and augment this work rather than repeat it.

About the Office

Location: The assignment is expected to be primarily remote, with the allocation of days and any travel agreed at contracting.

Overview

DNDi seeks an experienced consultant to advise senior colleagues and guide the development of its approach to multilateral development banks and related global health financing mechanisms. Building on existing analysis and relationships, the consultant will help DNDi prioritise opportunities, advance one major partnership and establish a practical plan for further engagement.

Responsibilities

  • Refine the strategic approach and develop an action plan. Assess priorities and demand in a selected set of countries and regional programmes, drawing on existing evidence, DNDi colleagues and targeted consultations. Review and, where needed, augment the country and development-bank analysis already undertaken, and use it to test and agree priorities with senior colleagues, within the direction outlined in this brief and DNDi’s capacity-sharing strategy.
  • Review DNDi’s existing outlines for several potential major programmes, including the capabilities DNDi and prospective partners could contribute to country-led health-system strengthening, and assess their feasibility, strategic fit and potential routes to MDB financing. Refine these approaches as appropriate.
  • Advance one major partnership. Guide and work alongside DNDi colleagues and prospective partners to develop a programme responding to country priorities, potentially across several countries. Clarify intended outcomes, country ownership, partner roles, an indicative budget and practical routes through which partners could be funded or contracted. Support consultations and agreed next steps in programme preparation.
  • Provide strategic and practical advice on advancing selected existing opportunities where the consultant’s expertise and networks can add value.

Initial areas of interest include pandemic and epidemic preparedness, clinical research capacity strengthening, and climate-sensitive diseases such as dengue. The consultant should bring broad global health judgement and flexibility to develop approaches with partners across prevention, preparedness and access.

Expected outputs

  • A concise strategy and action plan with priorities, responsibilities, resource needs and decision points.
  • One developed partnership concept, with partner roles, an indicative financing approach and documented next steps and responsibilities for further preparation.
  • A prioritised opportunity pipeline and outreach plan, with initial engagement and clear next steps.

Duration and level of effort

Approximately 40–45 working days over six months, with the allocation of days and any travel agreed at contracting.

Reporting line & Interactions

The consultant will work with a designated DNDi focal point and senior resource mobilisation, regional and technical colleagues. Regional colleagues will bring country knowledge and relationships and take opportunities forward with the consultant’s guidance. The consultant will maintain momentum through strategic advice, practical preparation and coordination of agreed actions.

Responsibilities will be agreed according to the opportunity: the consultant may advise colleagues, work alongside them or lead workshops and programme-development meetings. External engagement will be coordinated with DNDi relationship owners. DNDi will retain decisions on priorities and commitments.

Detailed scientific and sectoral expertise will be available from DNDi colleagues and partners.

Experience and Education

The assignment requires the experience and judgement to advise senior colleagues, guide practical programme development and lead workshops or meetings when needed.

Essential experience and capabilities

  • Strong global health expertise and understanding of country priorities and health systems in low- and middle-income countries.
  • Demonstrated experience working with at least one relevant multilateral development bank, including country engagement, financing mechanisms and programme preparation processes.
  • A record of taking programmes or partnerships from initial discussions into concrete development or implementation, involving governments, international organisations, technical institutions or delivery partners.
  • Ability to turn technical inputs into coherent programme concepts, indicative budgets and actionable plans; strong facilitation and clear, concise English drafting.

Desirable experience

  • Experience in epidemic preparedness, climate and health, neglected diseases.
  • Understanding of clinical research, pharmaceutical development, regulatory systems or medical-product access, and relevant development bank and global health networks.

Skills and competencies

The consultant may be based in any location, but must be able to work effectively across Asian, African and European time zones.

Other requirements

  • Fluency in English

Application

Please submit a CV, a brief proposed approach, examples of relevant programmes or partnerships advanced, availability and a financial proposal specifying the daily rate and proposed number of days.

You’ll gather and synthesize clinical information, evaluate diagnostic criteria and functional impairment, identify safety concerns and relevant differential diagnoses, and help families understand the most appropriate next steps in care.

Role Title: Law Review Cite-Checker

Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: $50–80/hour

Your tasks: Review citation-checking rubrics and build sample cite-checking tasks

Job Description

micro1 is engaging law students and recent law graduates with law journal experience to support a legal citation project. If you’ve spent time cite-checking for a law review or journal, this is that skill applied to a new context. No prior AI experience is required — your Bluebook fluency and editorial judgment are what matter.

Scope of Work

  1. Review existing Bluebook and pincite grading rubrics, and flag rules that are unclear, incomplete, or would be applied inconsistently by different editors.
  2. Identify edge cases the rubrics don’t currently cover and recommend how they should be handled.
  3. Create sample cite-checking tasks: source material paired with citations containing realistic errors, along with the correct answer and an explanation of the rule involved.
  4. Build tasks across a range of citation types and difficulty levels, from straightforward formatting errors to subtle pincite and source-support problems.
  5. Apply Bluebook rules consistently across all submissions.
  6. Flag ambiguous cases to project coordinators instead of resolving them silently.
  7. Deliver assigned work on schedule and at the required quality level.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Current law student (2L, 3L) or recent JD graduate.
  2. Law review or law journal experience, ideally including a cite-checking or source-collection role.
  3. Strong working knowledge of The Bluebook, including pincites, short forms, signals, and parentheticals.
  4. Able to explain why a citation is wrong, not just that it is — the reasoning matters as much as the correction.
  5. Careful and consistent across long sessions of detailed review work.
  6. Comfortable working independently and meeting deadlines without close supervision.
  7. Experience as a journal editor, articles editor, or executive editor is a plus.

How the selection process works

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions
  2. Complete the AI interview— this is how we showcase your skills to the client

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

About the role

BLP only works when it talks to our customers’ ERP systems. As an Integration Engineer, you build and own those connections and keep live integrations running for enterprise customers. Every new ERP system is a new problem to solve. You’ll lead our Oracle integrations across Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite and JD Edwards, while also contributing to other integrations.

What you’ll do

  • Own our integrations with Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite and JD Edwards and ensure their market fit, usability and reliability.

  • Design and implement interfaces for diverse protocols: REST, SOAP, direct DB access and file transfers.

  • Explore new ERP systems and determine the best way to connect them.

  • Build new ERP integrations, often in close collaboration with pilot customers.

  • Own existing integrations end to end, including issue resolution, and document them so teammates can pick them up.

  • Enable technical project managers to consult on, install and configure mature integrations.

What you'll bring

  • Hands-on integration experience with Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite or JD Edwards EnterpriseOne, ideally more than one. You have built or maintained interfaces yourself, not only used the system as a functional consultant or key user.

  • Experience with the native interfaces of at least one of these:

    • Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP: REST and SOAP web services, File-Based Data Import (FBDI) through the ERP Integration Service, and data extraction with BI Publisher or BI Cloud Connector (BICC).

    • NetSuite: SuiteTalk REST and SOAP web services, SuiteQL, SuiteScript 2.x (e.g., RESTlets, Map/Reduce scripts), and Token-Based Authentication or OAuth 2.0.

    • JD Edwards EnterpriseOne: AIS Server and Orchestrator, Business Services (BSSV), and Z-file interface tables (e.g., F0411Z1) with their batch processors.

  • A good understanding of purchase-to-pay data in Oracle ERPs: suppliers, purchase orders, receipts and supplier invoice matching.

  • Solid programming skills in at least one backend language. We build our integrations in Go. If you come from Java, C#, Python or similar and are keen to pick up Go, that works for us.

  • A degree in computer science or a related field, or equivalent experience.

  • A structured, self-reliant way of working, and ideally experience in a client-facing role.

  • Fluent English. German is a plus, as most of our customers are in the DACH region.

Nice to have:

  • Experience with both cloud (Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite) and on-premise (JD Edwards) environments, and the constraints of each (e.g., no direct database access in Fusion, governance limits in NetSuite).

  • Extensive experience with SQL, common data formats (JSON, XML, CSV) and transports (REST/SOAP APIs, SFTP).

  • Familiarity with modern engineering practices: Git, code reviews, automated testing and CI/CD.

  • Integration experience with other ERPs, such as SAP, Microsoft Dynamics or Infor.

Integration Engineer or Senior Integration Engineer

We hire at both levels. Four things decide where you start: years of experience, breadth of experience, coaching experience and scope.

Integration Engineer

  • Years: 2+ years of hands-on integration work, including Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite or JD Edwards.

  • Breadth: in-depth experience with one Oracle ERP and its interfaces.

  • Coaching: you learn quickly from senior colleagues and share what you learn with the team.

  • Scope: you deliver and maintain integrations and resolve issues independently, with guidance on architecture decisions.

Senior Integration Engineer

  • Years: 5+ years of hands-on integration work, several of them with Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite or JD Edwards.

  • Breadth: integration experience across two or more of Fusion, NetSuite and JD Edwards, or across Oracle and other ERPs, in cloud and on-premise environments.

Why BLP

Job Summary

We are seeking a Research Operations Analyst to support a multi-year mineral title consolidation program for one of the largest royalty funds in the United States.

This is a program-scale, long-term engagement that spans the full retitling pipeline- from title research through revenue recovery. The role begins with a strong focus on chain-of-title research, but is designed as an entry point into a broader operational career path across adjacent functions including curative resolution, owner communications, recording operations, and revenue administration.

The ideal candidate combines the analytical rigor of a legal researcher, the precision of a data analyst, and the operational adaptability to learn and execute across evolving workflows.

  • Conduct structured chain-of-title research for owner/fund pairs, tracing ownership histories from current ownership back to origin.
  • Review and interpret legal documents including deeds, probate filings, court orders, affidavits, conveyance instruments, and powers of attorney.
  • Cross-reference ownership data across multiple sources (county records, ownership registers, transfer histories) to verify accuracy and identify discrepancies.
  • Identify and document title gaps, ownership defects, missing documents, inflated decimals, and chain breaks, and flag issues for review and resolution.
  • Classify ownership records using the program's A/B classification framework (clean title vs. curative required).

  • Maintain consistent productivity against defined throughput benchmarks, with improving efficiency over time.
  • Follow established research methodologies, SOPs, and workflow protocols, and incorporate feedback to continuously improve accuracy.
  • Cross-train into additional operational functions over time, including curative resolution, owner communications, recording operations, operator engagement, and revenue transition workflows, following structured training and competency assessments.

Qualifications

The University of Notre Dame Australia is a Catholic university with campuses in Fremantle, Broome and Sydney. The Objects of the University are the provision of university education within a context of Catholic faith and values and the provision of an excellent standard of teaching, scholarship and research, training for the professions and the pastoral care of its students.

PhD Scholarship,Full-Time, budgeted $42,440 for 3 years not indexed annually.

Proposed start date January 2027.

About the Scholarship

This scholarship is based at the School of Medicine (Sydney campus) at the University of Notre Dame Australia. The applicant does not need to be on site. There is limited scope for the successful candidate to design their own research question, but it must be aligned with the wider project goals of examining the healthcare needs of rural people with intellectual disability as they grow older. It is well established that there are substantial inequalities in service provision for people with intellectual disability, particularly in non-metropolitan Australia. The complex needs of this population remain largely hidden and overlooked within the wider research agenda, leading to both inequality and inequity.

The successful candidate would be working within an established research group including experienced disability researchers acrossa number ofuniversities, other PhD candidates, disability support organisations and people with lived experience of intellectual disability. The project is also overseen by a dedicated project manager to support administrative process and day-to-day activities.

The PhD scholarship will support the mixed method research component of the MRFF-funded project that will explore polypharmacy in older people with intellectual disability and include quantitative analysis of survey data and follow up interviews with older adults with intellectual disability and their carers - across regional and rural regions of Australia. Findings from this research willinform the development and evaluation of a nurse-led intervention in the project's final stages. The work is embedded within a co-designed, participatory research approach that prioritises lived experience and community partnership.

Please note that the standard duration of candidature is 3 years full-time. If the extension of candidature is approved, the stipend will not be extended.

Your Role
The Medical Coder-Inpatient DRG (IPDRG) provides high-level technical competency and subject matter expertise in analyzing physician/provider documentation in Inpatient health records to determine the principal diagnosis, secondary diagnoses, principal procedure, and secondary procedures. Assigns appropriate Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Groups (MS-DRG), All Patient Refined DRGs (APR), Present on Admission (POA), as well as Severity of Illness (SOI) & Risk of Mortality (ROM) indicators for Inpatient records. Identifies Hospital Acquired Conditions (HAC) and Patient Safety Indicators (PSI) to ensure accurate hospital reimbursement.

As a Medical Coder - Inpatient, you will:

Documentation Review and Code Assignment

  • Assign appropriate code(s) by utilizing coding guidelines established by:
    • The Centers for Disease Control (CDC), ICD-CM Official Coding Guidelines for Coding and Reporting, Centers for Medicare/Medicaid Services (CMS) ICD-PCS Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting
    • American Hospital Association (AHA) Coding Clinic for International Classification of Diseases, Clinical Modification
    • American Health Information Management Association (AHIMA) Standards of Ethical Coding
    • Revenue Excellence/HM coding procedures and guidelines
  • Navigate the patient health record and other computer systems/sources to accurately determine diagnosis and procedures codes, MS-DRGs, APR DRGs, and identify HACs and PSIs or other indicators that could impact quality data and hospital reimbursement.
  • Code Inpatient health records utilizing encoder software and consistently uses online tools to support the coding process and references to assign ICD codes, MS-DRG, APR DRGs, POA, SOI & ROM indicators.
  • Review Inpatient health record documentation, as part of the coding process, to assess the presence of clinical evidence/indicators to support diagnosis code and MS-DRG, APR DRG assignments to potentially decrease denials.
  • Work on inpatient claim edits and may code consecutive/combined accounts to comply with the 72-hour rule and other account combine scenarios.
  • Adhere to the Inpatient coding quality and productivity standards established by the organization.
  • Safeguard patient health information in compliance with HIPAA standards.

Query Management & Follow-Up

  • Demonstrate knowledge of current, compliant coder query practices when consulting with physicians, Clinical Documentation Specialists (CDS) or other healthcare providers when additional information is needed for coding and/or to clarify conflicting or ambiguous documentation.
  • Utilize EMR communication tools to track missing documentation or Inpatient queries that require follow-up to facilitate coding in a timely fashion.

HIM Collaboration

  • Work with HIM and Patient Financial Services (PFS) teams, when needed, to help resolve billing, claims, denial, and appeals issues affecting reimbursement.

Coding Knowledge & Expertise

  • Maintain CEUs as appropriate for coding credentials as required by credentialing associations.
  • Maintain current knowledge of changes in Inpatient coding and reimbursement guidelines and regulations, as well as new applications or settings for Inpatient coding e.g., Hospital at Home.
  • Identify and report coding and/or EMR workflow issues to their supervisor.
  • Exhibit awareness of health record documentation or other coding ethics concerns. Notifies appropriate leadership for assistance and resolution when appropriate.
  • Maintain a working knowledge of applicable coding and reimbursement Federal, State, and local laws and regulations, Code of Ethics, as well as other policies and procedures in order to ensure adherence in a manner that reflects honest, ethical, and professional behavior.
  • Perform abstracting of additional data elements.

Other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

  • Credential/Certification: ActiveCertified Coding Specialist (CCS) or Certified Inpatient Coder (CIC), or Certified Documentation Improvement Practitioner (CDIP)

Must be proficient in identifying POA, SOI, and ROM indicators for Inpatient records as well as HACs and PSIs to ensure accurate hospital reimbursement. Familiarity with HIPAA regulations.

Preferred skills/expertise

Proficiency with Microsoft Office suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook, SharePoint). Proficiency with Microsoft Office suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook, SharePoint)

DoorDash's Red Team exists to find critical attack paths before real adversaries do. We're looking for a leader who can take this team to the next level.

We need an offensive security leader who stays close to the work. As the Engineering Manager of the Red Team, you'll inherit an existing team, level it up, expand headcount, and build the partnerships needed to turn red team findings into real engineering change. This is a player-coach role — you'll set strategic direction while staying hands-on with engagement scoping, tradecraft, and tooling decisions.

You'll report to the Director of Global Security Services.

What You’ll Do

  • The partner’s day. Complex, multi-time-zone diaries: schedule, protect, and make the call when two things collide. Inboxes with judgment, not just volume: triage, surface, draft the first pass, chase what has gone quiet. Meeting packs, briefing notes, agendas, and the follow-up actions afterwards. Travel end to end, including the changes in flight and the reconciliation afterwards.

  • Strong proficiency with MS Office, Aderant or similar practice management software, PowerBI or similar data analytics dashboards, Claude, CoPilot or similar AI tools, Asana or similar project management tools

  • Ability to remain poised under pressure, multitask, and prioritize effectively
  • Strong team orientation and a preference for collaboration
  • Experience with a practice management, billing, time-capture or document management system — or evidence you have learned a comparable system quickly

Role Overview:
The Care Coordinator plays a key role in supporting older people receiving Home Care Package and Support at Home services to live safely, independently, and with dignity in their own homes. This role is responsible for delivering high-quality service coordination, including client onboarding, scheduling and rostering, referral management, documentation, and clear, respectful communication with clients, families, and providers. The Care Coordinator ensures that services are organised, goal-aligned, culturally inclusive, and responsive to each client's needs and preferences, while upholding the principles of supported decision-making, wellness, reablement, and dignity of risk
In managing a caseload of clients with low to moderately complex needs, the Care Coordinator also performs key functions such as gathering information for assessments and care plans, identifying early signs of deterioration, supporting risk assessments, coordinating care plan reviews, and monitoring service outcomes to ensure safety and quality. The role promotes trauma-informed, culturally safe practice in all interactions and collaborates closely with the broader team to ensure compliance with organisational policies, WHS requirements, and quality and safety standards. Through these responsibilities, the Care Coordinator contributes to a high-performing, client-centred service model that delivers consistent, safe, and effective Support at Home services

What﻿ You'll Do:

﻿﻿

1. Client Onboarding & Initial Information Gathering
  • Conduct onboarding intake and complete client setup in the care management system.
  • Gather all relevant documentation, including health summaries, hospital discharge notes, allied health recommendations, cultural needs, identity preferences, communication needs, and existing informal/formal supports.
  • Explain the Support at Home program, service list, approved supports, pricing structure, rights, responsibilities, and the client's Support Plan in a clear, trauma-informed manner.
  • Ensure all onboarding interactions reflect:
    • trauma-informed communication
    • culturally safe practice
    • supported decision-making
    • respect for identity, autonomy, and dignity
    • transparent discussion of services and options
  • Identify any risks or early signs of deterioration during onboarding and escalate promptly.
  • Support the client to understand and complete care planning documents
Outcome: Clients feel respected, understood, informed, culturally supported, and emotionally safe from the first point of contact.
2. Supporting Care Planning & Reassessment
  • Gather information for assessments across functional, clinical, social, cultural, environmental, behavioural, and safety domains.
  • Support the development and review of Individualised Support Plans and quarterly budgets, ensuring goals and preferences are documented using supported decision-making principles.
  • Assist clients to understand their plan, budget, approved services, and care options.
  • Coordinate and schedule reassessments when:
    • needs evolve
    • conditions change
    • goals have been met or require updating
    • emerging risks or deterioration is identified
  • Assist in collecting risk information, documenting risk themes, and contributing to risk mitigation strategies under clinical direction.
  • Ensure all plan updates reflect wellness and reablement principles.
3. Monitoring of Wellbeing, Risks & Early Deterioration
  • Conduct monthly client touchpoints early in the care journey and additional monitoring as clinically appropriate.
  • Monitor client wellbeing by communicating with clients, workers, family members, supporters, and providers.
  • Identify early signs of deterioration (physical, cognitive, emotional, social) and escalate promptly.
  • Support updating of risk profiles, safety plans, and care plans following clinical direction.
  • Assist in implementing and tracking risk mitigation strategies over time.
  • Review client notes regularly to identify changing needs or risks.
  • Record incidents and assist with follow-up documentation (not investigation, which is excluded)
4. Coordination of Services, Rostering & Scheduling
  • Coordinating the safe, timely commencement of services following onboarding.
  • Communicating service preferences, cultural needs, worker preferences, and schedule options to the rostering team
  • Communicating with support workers, allied health clinicians, nursing staff, and external providers about client needs and wellbeing.
  • Issuing internal and external referrals in line with SaH rules and client needs.
  • Organising approved aids, equipment, and consumables within SaH/HCP guidelines.
  • Supporting continuity of care and ensuring clients are notified of service changes.
  • Facilitating transitions in/out of hospital, respite, short term restorative care, or other settings and ensuring continuity of care through timely communication and documentation.
5. Client & Family Communication
  • Provide respectful, trauma-informed, culturally safe, and transparent communication with clients and families.
  • Support clients to understand their service options, risks, and preferences using supported decision-making principles.
  • Arrange interpreters, translated materials, and communication aids when required.
  • Assist clients to express feedback
  • Maintain accurate, real-time progress notes and documentation.
Outcome: Clients and families feel heard, supported, informed, and empowered.
6. Monthly Client Touchpoints & Feedback Collection
  • Conduct or coordinate monthly touchpoints during initial engagement or when clinically appropriate thereafter.
  • Collect and document client feedback, themes, issues, preferences, and suggestions.
  • Escalate concerns promptly to senior staff.
  • Identify opportunities to increase wellness- and goal-aligned service utilisation.
7. Budget & Financial Support Activities
  • Monitor client budgets.
  • Identify and flag risks of overspending and support corrective planning.
  • Assist in ordering approved consumables in line with SaH/HCP inclusion rules.
  • Resolve billing questions with the finance team.
  • Identify opportunities to maximise reablement-aligned service delivery within budget.
  • Prepare budget summaries for quarterly review.
8. Quality, Safety, Compliance & Organisational Contribution
  • Maintain accurate, high-quality documentation and ensure digital integrity in our compliance software Visual Care.
  • Promote a safe reporting culture free from fear of retaliation.
  • Support WHS, infection control, safe environment practices, and hazard identification.
  • Participate in quality audits, reviews, incidents follow-up, and improvement activities.
  • Ensure compliance with:
    • Aged Care Act 2024
    • Strengthened Quality Standards
    • Aged Care Code of Conduct
    • Statement of Rights
    • Organisational policies
  • Support improvements in care processes, service delivery, and client experience.
9. Relationship Building & Stakeholder Engagement
  • Build trusting, respectful relationships with clients, families, advocates, and supporters.
  • Liaise with external providers to ensure coordinated, high-quality service delivery.
  • Participate in multidisciplinary meetings, internal case discussions, and handovers.
  • Promote Sensible Care services ethically and professionally
What﻿ You'll Do:
Essential
  • Excellent Communication Skills in English (Written and Verbal):
    Ability to communicate effectively and politely with clients, team members, healthcare professionals, and external service providers.
  • Background in healthcare and nursing is highly regarded
  • Sound understanding of community healthcare and/or aged care services
  • Time Management and Planning:
    Strong time management skills to handle multiple tasks, meet deadlines, and manage competing priorities effectively.
  • Interpersonal Skills:
    Ability to develop and maintain positive relationships within the team, with clients, service providers, and other stakeholders.
  • Attention to Detail:
    High level of accuracy in documenting client information, service updates, and other essential data in the systems.
  • Computer Proficiency:
    Competence in using general computer applications, with a willingness to learn our care management software package, including Sensible Care's care management software Visual Care.
  • Compliance Requirements:
    The role requires the successful candidate to have or obtain a national police check due to the management nature of the position in the aged care sector.
  • Compliance with Aged Care Act 2024, Code of Conduct, Statement of Rights, and all Sensible Care policies
  • Adherence to WHS and infection control requirements

jobs.excerpt: About this RoleWe're looking for a Senior Creative Copywriter to bring Valerie's portfolio of consumer and eCommerce brands to life through exceptional writing, original ideas, and distinctive brand storytelling.
jobs.description:
About this Role

We're looking for a Senior Creative Copywriter to bring Valerie's portfolio of consumer and eCommerce brands to life through exceptional writing, original ideas, and distinctive brand storytelling.

This is a creative role first and foremost. You'll develop brand voices, campaign concepts, messaging frameworks, social content, performance ads, website copy, and CRM campaigns that connect with audiences while driving business results.

You'll work across multiple brands and international markets, collaborating closely with Creative Directors, Designers, Brand Growth Pods, Performance, and Web & Digital Experience teams. We want someone who can move seamlessly between building a brand's long-term identity and writing sharp, commercially effective copy for everyday campaigns.

Great copy starts with human insight, originality, cultural understanding, and a genuine command of language. AI can support your process, but we want someone who can think independently, challenge generic ideas, and create work that feels distinctly human.

Success in this role means distinctive brand voices, original creative concepts, culturally relevant messaging, exceptional writing quality, faster creative delivery, fewer revisions, and copy that contributes to both brand building and commercial performance.

You could be a great fit if...

  • You see copywriting as a craft and care deeply about the quality, originality, and impact of your words.

  • You can turn consumer insights and brand strategy into compelling stories, campaign ideas, and messaging.

  • You have a strong conceptual mind and enjoy contributing ideas beyond the brief.

  • You understand how to balance brand storytelling with performance marketing and commercial objectives.

  • You have an exceptional command of English, including nuance, humour, idioms, and cultural references.

  • You can adapt your writing for different brands, audiences, platforms, and international markets.

  • You know how to make product benefits compelling without making the copy sound forced or salesy.

  • You challenge generic messaging and know when something sounds artificial, overused, or off-brand.

  • You're comfortable managing multiple brands and briefs without compromising on quality.

  • You enjoy collaborating with creative, design, strategy, and performance teams and can confidently explain your creative choices.

  • You use AI thoughtfully for research and exploration but can develop strong creative work independently.

  • You're proactive, receptive to feedback, and take ownership of your work from the first idea to final delivery.

Requirements

  • 5–7+ years of experience in creative copywriting, ideally within advertising, branding, creative agencies, or consumer-focused businesses.

  • An exceptional portfolio demonstrating original thinking, strong writing craft, and versatility across different brands and formats.

  • Outstanding written English, with a sophisticated understanding of tone, storytelling, grammar, and language.

  • Strong cultural understanding of English-speaking markets, particularly the US, UK, and Australia.

  • Experience developing brand narratives, tone-of-voice guidelines, messaging frameworks, and brand books.

  • Proven ability to conceptualise and write campaign ideas, headlines, taglines, and product launch messaging.

  • Hands-on experience writing for organic social, paid advertising, creator content, websites, landing pages, eCommerce, and CRM.

  • Understanding of how copy contributes to brand building, customer acquisition, engagement, and conversion.

  • Ability to adapt messaging for platforms such as Meta, TikTok, Google, and YouTube.

  • Good understanding of SEO, CRO, creative testing, and performance-led messaging.

  • Excellent editorial judgement, attention to detail, and ownership of final copy quality.

  • Ability to collaborate with Creative Directors, Designers, Strategists, and Performance specialists.

  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple brands, deadlines, and competing priorities.

  • A collaborative, proactive mindset with the ability to work independently and incorporate feedback.

  • Genuine curiosity about language, culture, advertising, and consumer behaviour.

  • Ability to use AI as a supporting tool without relying on AI-generated drafts as a substitute for original creative thinking.

Bonus Points

  • Experience working with eCommerce, D2C, lifestyle, beauty, fashion, wellness, or other consumer brands.

  • Experience building brands from the ground up or working in fast-growing, founder-led environments.

  • Experience developing creative territories and integrated campaigns across multiple channels.

  • Experience writing for international audiences and adapting messaging across markets.

  • Experience collaborating with performance teams on creative experiments, A/B testing, and messaging optimisation.

  • Familiarity with creator partnerships, influencer campaigns, and short-form video scripts.

  • Experience building copywriting guidelines, editorial standards, and reusable messaging frameworks.

  • Experience using AI tools and automation to improve research, ideation, and creative workflows while maintaining originality.

You probably shouldn't apply if...

  • Your experience is primarily limited to content execution, blogs, or SEO articles without strong creative copywriting.

  • You rely on templates, familiar advertising clichés, or AI-generated drafts rather than developing original ideas.

  • You struggle to demonstrate your writing ability through a strong portfolio.

  • You have limited experience developing brand voices, campaign concepts, or messaging frameworks.

  • Your writing is grammatically correct but lacks personality, nuance, cultural understanding, or originality.

  • You focus only on creative expression without considering the audience, business objective, or commercial outcome.

  • You struggle to adapt your writing for different brands, platforms, or international audiences.

  • You prefer working on one brand or brief at a time and find multiple concurrent projects challenging.

  • You're uncomfortable explaining your creative decisions, collaborating with other teams, or incorporating feedback.

  • You view copywriting as simply putting words together rather than solving communication and brand challenges.

The best time to join Valerie was yesterday. The next best time is now 🤓

👋Our Hiring Process

We want interviews to be valuable for both sides. Throughout the process, you'll meet the people you'll work with, learn more about the role, and get a chance to understand how we think and operate.

Our process typically includes:

  • Introductory conversation with our Talent team <> 30 mins

  • Hiring Manager interview <> 30-45 mins

  • Role-specific assessment or practical exercise (where applicable)

  • Cross-functional or stakeholder interviews <> 30-45 mins

  • Final conversation with leadership <> 30-45 mins

We'll always let you know what to expect before each stage.

💪🏾What You Can Expect

  • Meaningful work with visible impact

  • High ownership from day one

  • Collaboration with experienced founders, operators, and specialists

  • A team that values curiosity, initiative, and continuous improvement

  • Competitive compensation and the tools you need to do your best work

  • Opportunities to grow as Valerie grows

Valerie is committed to building an inclusive workplace where people from different backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives can thrive. We hire based on skills, potential, and the ability to contribute to our team.

jobs.excerpt: Talent Acquisition Specialist SnapshotCurvion Blue is looking for a Talent Acquisition Specialist who knows how to find, assess, and attract high-performing sales talent.
jobs.description:
Talent Acquisition Specialist Snapshot

Curvion Blue is looking for a Talent Acquisition Specialist who knows how to find, assess, and attract high-performing sales talent.

This isn't a traditional HR recruiting role where you're posting jobs, waiting for applications, and hoping the right person wanders into the funnel.

You're going to be responsible for building and managing talent pipelines for sales roles across our business, with a heavy focus on identifying A-Players who can perform in high-ticket sales environments.

The ideal candidate has experience in Talent Acquisition or recruiting and understands how to source, qualify, interview, and move candidates through a high-volume hiring process.

Bonus points if you've actually sold before. Extra bonus points if you've sold high-ticket.

We want someone who understands salespeople because they've been one, worked closely with them, or recruited them extensively.

Position Overview

As a Talent Acquisition Specialist, you will own recruiting across Curvion Blue's sales organization and help us continuously build a bench of exceptional talent.

You'll work closely with leadership to understand what "great" looks like for each role, then take that profile into the market and find the people who match it.

This is a hands-on recruiting role for someone who enjoys sourcing, talking to candidates, assessing talent, and moving quickly.

You will be responsible for the full recruiting lifecycle, including sourcing, candidate outreach, screening, interview coordination, candidate evaluation, pipeline management, and offer management.

More importantly, you'll become an expert in identifying the difference between someone who sounds like a great salesperson and someone who can actually perform.

Your Core Responsibilities

Talent Sourcing

  • Build proactive talent pipelines for closers, setters, sales leaders, and other revenue-generating roles.

  • Source candidates through LinkedIn, job boards, referrals, communities, databases, and creative outbound strategies.

  • Develop targeted sourcing strategies based on role requirements and candidate profiles.

  • Continuously build talent pools rather than starting from zero every time a role opens.

Candidate Qualification

  • Conduct recruiter screens to evaluate experience, communication, motivation, sales ability, and overall fit.

  • Identify candidates with demonstrated performance rather than relying solely on resume keywords.

  • Assess candidates against defined scorecards and role-specific success profiles.

  • Understand sales metrics, quotas, KPIs, close rates, lead flow, revenue, and other performance indicators.

  • Identify red flags and know when to move a candidate forward versus cut them from the process.

Sales Talent Acquisition

  • Become deeply familiar with high-ticket sales roles and the characteristics of top-performing setters, closers, sales directors, and sales leaders.

  • Understand the difference between legitimate sales experience and resume fluff.

  • Build relationships with high-performing sales professionals and maintain a warm talent network.

  • Help Curvion Blue become known as a destination for high-performing sales talent.

Candidate Experience

  • Own candidate communication throughout the recruiting process.

  • Keep candidates engaged, informed, and moving through each stage.

  • Represent Curvion Blue professionally and enthusiastically.

  • Create a candidate experience that reflects the level of talent we want to attract.

Recruiting Operations

  • Maintain accurate candidate data and pipeline stages in our ATS.

  • Track recruiting metrics including pipeline volume, conversion rates, time-to-fill, source performance, and quality of hire.

  • Coordinate interviews, skills assessments, roleplays, and other evaluation stages.

  • Partner with hiring managers to continuously improve the recruiting process.

  • Identify bottlenecks and recommend ways to improve recruiting efficiency.

Hiring & Onboarding Partnership

  • Support offer creation and candidate closing.

  • Help ensure strong candidates remain engaged through acceptance and start date.

  • Partner with the team to identify early indicators of successful hires.

  • Track quality of hire and use performance data to improve future recruiting decisions.

You SHOULD Apply If

  • You have 1+ years of Talent Acquisition, recruiting, or full-cycle recruiting experience.

  • You have experience recruiting salespeople, preferably revenue-generating roles.

  • You know how to source candidates rather than relying exclusively on inbound applicants.

  • You're comfortable conducting candidate screens and making recommendations to hiring managers.

  • You can quickly identify whether someone's experience actually matches what they're claiming.

  • You are highly comfortable talking to salespeople.

  • You understand performance-driven environments and aren't intimidated by metrics.

  • You can manage multiple open roles without losing track of candidates or details.

  • You're organized, responsive, and operationally strong.

  • You're comfortable working in an environment where priorities can move quickly.

  • You can communicate professionally with candidates at every level.

  • You're proactive. If you see a recruiting problem, your instinct is to solve it rather than wait for someone to tell you what to do.

BIG BONUS POINTS

  • You have past sales experience.

  • You have high-ticket sales experience.

  • You've been a setter, closer, AE, sales manager, or sales leader.

  • You've recruited high-ticket closers or setters before.

  • You've worked in coaching, consulting, SaaS, agency, or other performance-driven sales environments.

  • You understand sales compensation structures and can speak intelligently about earning potential with candidates.

  • You have an established network of sales talent.

  • You've recruited for remote sales organizations.

You SHOULD NOT Apply If

  • You only want to work inbound applications.

  • You don't enjoy outbound sourcing.

  • You need every step of your day mapped out for you.

  • You don't like metrics or performance accountability.

  • You're uncomfortable making judgment calls on candidates.

  • You struggle to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.

  • You view recruiting as simply scheduling interviews and forwarding resumes.

  • You don't enjoy talking to people.

  • You're looking for a slow-moving corporate environment with six approval layers before anything gets done.

  • You have never recruited before and are looking for your first opportunity in Talent Acquisition.

Long-Term

You become one of the people Curvion Blue relies on to answer:

"We need five great salespeople. Where are they?"

And your answer is:

"Already working on it."

The Person We're Looking For

We're not looking for someone who simply wants to "work in HR."

We're looking for a talent hunter.

Someone who enjoys the chase.

Someone who can look at a LinkedIn profile and immediately start thinking:

"This person might be good. Let me find out."

You should enjoy talking to people, asking good questions, spotting potential, and figuring out what makes someone tick.

You should be competitive enough to care about winning the search, analytical enough to care about hiring quality, and organized enough to keep the machine running.

If you've sold before, you'll probably have a natural advantage here because you already understand how to build rapport, overcome objections, create urgency, and influence decisions.

If you've sold high-ticket, even better. You already understand the world our candidates operate in.

At Curvion Blue, we're building revenue engines for our clients. That requires exceptional people.

Your job is to help us find them.

Schedule:

  • Monday to Friday

  • 9AM - 6 PM (specific to your time zone)

Compensation Range: $50K - $80K

Staff Software Engineer (AI Evals)

Contract | $100–$200/hour | 20-40 hrs/week | Start ASAP

We’re looking for highly experienced software engineer to help evaluate the quality of interactions with modern coding agents such as OpenAI Codex and Claude Code.

This is not a traditional engineering role.

You won’t be writing production code.

You’ll be evaluating something harder: whether the model thinks like a great engineer.

What This Role Actually Is

You will assess how AI coding agents behave in real-world scenarios — focusing on:

  • Whether the response makes sense

  • Whether the preamble and reasoning are useful

  • Whether the output reflects strong engineering judgment

  • Whether the interaction feels right to an experienced developer

This role is about engineering taste — not syntax correctness.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Evaluate AI-generated coding interactions end-to-end

  • Judge whether outputs are:

    • Useful

    • Correct (at a high level)

    • Aligned with how a strong engineer would think

  • Assess the quality of explanations and reasoning, not just code

  • Distinguish between different levels of response quality (e.g. what makes something a 2 vs 4)

  • Provide clear, opinionated feedback on:

    • What worked

    • What didn’t

    • What felt “off” or misleading

  • Help define what great looks like when interacting with tools like Cursor

What We Mean by “Taste”

We’re specifically looking for engineers who can answer questions like:

  • Does this feel like something a strong engineer would actually say?

  • Is this explanation helpful, or just technically correct?

  • Is the model guiding the user well, or just dumping output?

  • Would this interaction build or erode trust?

You should be comfortable making subjective but rigorous judgments.

Who You Are

  • Staff / Principal-level engineer (or equivalent experience)

  • Strong background in one of the below:

    • Go

    • Python

    • Rust

    • TypeScript / JavaScript

  • Hands-on experience using:

    • Claude Code

    • Cursor

  • Deep familiarity with modern AI-assisted dev workflows

  • Able to evaluate code without needing to fully execute or deeply review every line

  • Comfortable giving direct, opinionated feedback

  • High bar for what “good engineering” looks like

Nice to Have

  • Experience with tools like Cursor or similar AI-first IDEs

  • Prior exposure to prompt design or evaluation workflows

  • Experience mentoring senior engineers or defining engineering standards

Engagement Details

jobs.excerpt: About MenloMenlo Research is an Applied R&D lab building Asimov, an open-source humanoid robot platform, and the full software stack that powers it.
jobs.description:
About Menlo

Menlo Research is an Applied R&D lab building Asimov, an open-source humanoid robot platform, and the full software stack that powers it. Our mission is to make humanoid labor economically viable -- turning software into physical labor at scale. We build across the full stack: hardware architecture, locomotion, autonomy, simulation, and infrastructure. We move fast, ship to real robots, and open-source everything we can. If you want your work to matter beyond a paper or a demo, this is the place.

The Role

As an Electrical Engineer, you will own the design, integration, and bring-up of the electronic systems that power Asimov. From power distribution to motor control to sensor integration, you will work across schematics, PCB layouts, harness design, and hardware debug -- ensuring every electrical decision holds up in the field and integrates cleanly with the broader mechanical and firmware stack.

What You'll Do

  • Design and review schematics and PCB layouts for power distribution units, motor driver boards, and actuator control electronics

  • Integrate wiring harnesses, PCBA enclosures, and motor controllers into mechanical assemblies from the ground up

  • Lead bring-up of power systems, sensors, and actuator subassemblies; diagnose and resolve issues across multiple hardware revisions

  • Define and run electrical and system-level test protocols, analyze failure modes, and iterate based on test data

  • Work closely with firmware and controls teams to ensure electrical design choices support stable, low-latency control loops

  • Apply expertise in connector selection, grounding strategies, harness routing, and EMI suppression to ensure robust and field-reliable hardware

  • Contribute to Menlo's open-source design efforts, including PCB schematics and manufacturing documentation for the broader robotics community

What You'll Bring

  • 3 or more years of hands-on electrical engineering experience on high-complexity electromechanical products

  • Solid understanding of electrical and electronic systems, including motor drivers, sensors, and embedded hardware integration

  • Deep familiarity with low-voltage (under 60V) DC power systems, DC-DC converters, MOSFET gate drivers, current-sense amplifiers, and passive network design

  • Proficiency using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and CAN/UART sniffers for in-depth hardware debug

  • Expertise in connector selection, grounding strategies, harness routing, and EMI suppression techniques

  • Strong communication skills to drive alignment across firmware teams, mechanical engineers, and leadership

Bonus points for:

  • Experience with bipedal or humanoid robot hardware or legged locomotion platforms

  • Familiarity with CAN bus, motor controllers, and how electrical design choices affect firmware and control integration

  • Scripting experience in Python for hardware automation and data analysis

  • Familiarity with sim-to-real workflows and how hardware decisions affect locomotion policy training and transfer

Why Join Menlo?

You will be part of a tight-knit team defining the next generation of humanoid robots. With genuine ownership of the mechanical systems that bring Asimov to life, you will see your designs go from CAD to real-world deployments. If you thrive in fast-paced, open-collaborative environments, let's build the future of robotics together.

A Note on AI

You don't need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect everyone at Menlo to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement. When that's the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don't treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on.

Equal Opportunity and Accommodations

We hire talented people from a wide range of backgrounds. If you're excited about a role but don't meet every bullet, we still encourage you to apply. Menlo Research is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any legally protected characteristic. Menlo provides reasonable accommodations during the application process. If you need one, please let your recruiter know.

jobs.description:
About Abridge

Abridge was founded in 2018 with the mission of powering deeper understanding in healthcare. Our AI-powered platform was purpose-built for medical conversations, improving clinical documentation efficiencies while enabling clinicians to focus on what matters most—their patients.

Our enterprise-grade technology transforms patient-clinician conversations into structured clinical notes in real-time, with deep EMR integrations. Powered by Linked Evidence and our purpose-built, auditable AI, we are the only company that maps AI-generated summaries to ground truth, helping providers quickly trust and verify the output. As pioneers in generative AI for healthcare, we are setting the industry standards for the responsible deployment of AI across health systems.

We are a growing team of practicing MDs, AI scientists, PhDs, creatives, technologists, and engineers working together to empower people and make care make more sense. We have offices located in the Mission District in San Francisco, the SoHo neighborhood of New York, and East Liberty in Pittsburgh.

The Role

Abridge is seeking an experienced Privacy Counsel to lead our privacy team and scale our privacy and data governance program as the company grows. This is a highly visible role at the intersection of artificial intelligence, healthcare, data governance, data protection, and product innovation.

You will serve as a trusted legal advisor to senior leadership and partner closely with Security, Product, Engineering, and other cross-functional teams. You will provide practical, risk-based guidance, lead critical privacy and data initiatives, and build systems that enable Abridge to innovate responsibly while meeting evolving regulatory and customer expectations.

The ideal candidate brings deep privacy expertise, sound business judgment, and experience operating with autonomy and leading a team in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

What You’ll Do

  • Build Abridge’s privacy program, providing practical, product-focused counseling to the Security, Product and Engineering teams.

  • Advise teams on privacy laws related to artificial intelligence, machine learning, clinical data, product development, secondary use of data and the responsible use of sensitive information.

  • Help develop, maintain, and scale global privacy programs.

  • Support data sharing and ecosystem questions (first/third-party, vendors, partners, internal platform services), including governance and contractual expectations in partnership with commercial counsel.

  • Monitor and respond to changes in privacy laws and regulations, including AI regulations.

  • Draft, maintain, and operationalize privacy policies, playbooks, templates, governance standards, and training materials that promote awareness and consistent decision-making across the company.

  • Work cross functionally with talented product and engineering teams in evaluating the impact of privacy and data protection laws and regulatory guidance on exciting product developments.

What You’ll Bring

  • Have 10+ years of experience with a mix of in-house, health tech, or technology-focused law firm roles.

  • Experience building, developing, advising, and evaluating programs that ensure products comply with laws, regulations, and external commitments.

  • Knowledge of HIPAA and other healthcare privacy requirements, as well as CCPA/CPRA, biometric privacy laws, and applicable U.S. state privacy and data security frameworks.

  • A practical, risk-based approach and the ability to balance legal, regulatory, business, and customer considerations.

  • Strong business judgment and the ability to work independently in an environment that values autonomy, accountability, and trust.

  • Excellent communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to translate complex legal requirements into clear, actionable guidance for technical and nontechnical audiences.

  • Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple high-priority matters in a dynamic, fast-moving environment.

  • A Juris Doctor degree from an accredited law school and active membership in good standing with at least one U.S. state bar.

Bonus Points If…

  • Strong preference for prior experience on healthcare or health tech.

  • Familiarity with recent trends in the intersection of privacy regulations and artificial intelligence.

  • IAPP CIPP certification.

This is a hybrid role requiring employees to work from our SF or NYC office 3 days per week.

Why Work at Abridge?

At Abridge, we’re transforming healthcare delivery experiences with generative AI, enabling clinicians and patients to connect in deeper, more meaningful ways. Our mission is clear: to power deeper understanding in healthcare. We’re driving real, lasting change, with millions of medical conversations processed each month.

Joining Abridge means stepping into a fast-paced, high-growth startup where your contributions truly make a difference. Our culture requires extreme ownership—every employee has the ability to (and is expected to) make an impact on our customers and our business.

Beyond individual impact, you will have the opportunity to work alongside a team of curious, high-achieving people in a supportive environment where success is shared, growth is constant, and feedback fuels progress. At Abridge, it’s not just what we do—it’s how we do it. Every decision is rooted in empathy, always prioritizing the needs of clinicians and patients.

We’re committed to supporting your growth, both professionally and personally. Whether it's flexible work hours, an inclusive culture, or ongoing learning opportunities, we are here to help you thrive and do the best work of your life.

If you are ready to make a meaningful impact alongside passionate people who care deeply about what they do, Abridge is the place for you.

How we take care of Abridgers:

  • Generous Time Off: 14 paid holidays, flexible PTO for salaried employees, and accrued time off for hourly employees

  • Comprehensive Health Plans: Medical, Dental, and Vision coverage for all full-time employees and their families.

  • Generous HSA Contribution: If you choose a High Deductible Health Plan, Abridge makes monthly contributions to your HSA.

  • Paid Parental Leave: Generous paid parental leave for all full-time employees.

  • Family Forming Benefits: Resources and financial support to help you build your family.

  • 401(k) Matching: Contribution matching to help invest in your future.

  • Personal Device Allowance: Tax free funds for personal device usage.

  • Pre-tax Benefits: Access to Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) and Commuter Benefits.

  • Lifestyle Wallet: Monthly contributions for fitness, professional development, coworking, and more.

  • Mental Health Support: Dedicated access to therapy and coaching to help you reach your goals.

  • Sabbatical Leave: Paid Sabbatical Leave after 5 years of employment.

  • Compensation and Equity: Competitive compensation and equity grants for full time employees.

  • ... and much more!

Equal Opportunity Employer

Abridge is an equal opportunity employer and considers all qualified applicants equally without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, or disability.

We're committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the interview process. Once you submit your application, we'll follow up with details on how to request an accommodation for interviewing, completing any assessments, or otherwise participating in the selection process.

Staying safe - Protect yourself from recruitment fraud

We are aware of individuals and entities fraudulently representing themselves as Abridge recruiters and/or hiring managers. Abridge will never ask for financial information or payment, or for personal information such as bank account number or social security number during the job application or interview process. Any emails from the Abridge recruiting team will come from an @abridge.com email address. You can learn more about how to protect yourself from these types of fraud by referring to this article. Please exercise caution and cease communications if something feels suspicious about your interactions.

LaunchDarkly helps engineering organizations ship software and AI with speed, safety, and control. Our engineers build the systems, services, SDKs, developer tools, cloud infrastructure, and product experiences that make this possible. The work spans high-scale distributed systems, reliable data and event pipelines, intuitive enterprise workflows, and AI-powered capabilities that help teams manage the next generation of software delivery.

LaunchDarkly’s SDKs are used in systems that perform trillions of feature flag evaluations each day, giving our engineering work a direct connection to the reliability and customer experience of software around the world. As the company grows, we are expanding beyond traditional feature management into experimentation, observability, and AgentControl—helping customers control more of the software and AI lifecycle. That creates an unusually broad set of technical challenges, visible customer impact, and room for engineers to shape what comes next.

We believe in the power of teams. We work with humility, openness, curiosity, and care; we value clear communication, thoughtful technical judgment, inclusive collaboration, and a strong sense of ownership. LaunchDarkly serves trillions of feature flags daily to customers all around the globe, and every flag is handled by our SDKs. Job Summary:

About Live Nation:

Join the team at Live Nation, where innovation meets live entertainment on a global scale! With 40,000 shows and 500 million tickets sold each year, we’re the industry leader, powered by 44,000 talented individuals worldwide. At Live Nation, we’re passionate about transforming live events and creating extraordinary moments for artists, event professionals, and fans.

About the role:

Are you a calm and decisive professional with a passion for cybersecurity? Step into the role of Incident Response Lead and make an impact on a global scale. This is your chance to be on the front line of cyber defence, guiding teams through high-pressure security events and driving containment, eradication, and recovery efforts.

Working remotely, you’ll collaborate closely with technical experts and leadership across regions, ensuring alignment, clear communication, and swift decision-making during complex incidents. From leading evidence collection and reporting to shaping postmortems and training exercises, you’ll be the trusted subject matter expert steering the organisation through critical cyber challenges.

If you’re passionate about cybersecurity, thrive under pressure, and have what it takes to keep our global operations resilient, we’d love to hear from you. Apply with a cover letter highlighting why you’re the right person to lead us through high-pressure incidents.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Lead incident response: Drive containment, eradication, and recovery efforts during cyber events, ensuring timely and effective resolution.
  • Bridge communication: Act as liaison between technical teams and leadership, delivering clear updates and trusted guidance.
  • Collect and analyse evidence: Gather forensic artefacts, reconstruct attack chains, and provide expert input into investigations.
  • Deliver post-incident learning: Conduct postmortems, document lessons, and recommend improvements to strengthen resilience.
  • Develop stakeholder reporting: Create clear and concise incident reports, guidance, and updates for technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Promote readiness: Design and run tabletop exercises and workshops to build team capability and organisational awareness.
  • Collaborate globally: Work closely with regional peers as part of a 24/7 on-call rotation across a complex global enterprise.

What you’ll bring:

  • Proven cyber background: 5+ years in cybersecurity, including 3+ years in incident response, with proven event investigation experience.
  • Analytical mindset: Advanced ability to categorise, investigate, and resolve incidents while preserving evidence.
  • Tool proficiency: Hands-on experience with SIEM, IDS/IPS, EDR, cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP), and other defence technologies.
  • Resilient under pressure: Exceptional decision-making, problem-solving, and conflict management skills in high-stakes scenarios.

  • Access to concerts, events, and other entertainment perks.

  • A diverse, equitable workplace where every voice matters.
